Madhive is the leading independent and fully customizable operating system built to help local media professionals build profitable, differentiated, and efficient businesses. Madhive empowers sales teams to extend their reach into streaming and connects local advertisers with the communities they serve. Madhive’s platform provides the unique ability to reach local audiences at national scale, with premium supply partnerships and end-to-end tools for planning, targeting, and measuring full-funnel campaign outcomes. Powering campaigns for over 30,000 small and medium businesses per day, Madhive is driving the evolution of local media.
  
  
Madhive is looking for a
**Senior FP&A Associate**
to join our Strategic Finance team in New York. The successful candidate will own core forecasting, reporting, and business partnering infrastructure, directly informing pricing, investments, and stakeholder reporting.
  
  
This is a builder's role. You will design and automate maturing financial processes, establish operational standards, and communicate complex insights clearly across the business.
  
  
You will report to the Director, Strategic Finance and partner closely with all the departmental leaders across the business.
  
  
This role is based out of our New York City headquarters at 225 Broadway. We operate on a hybrid model, and the ideal candidate will work from the NYC office 3 days per week as needed for team collaboration, close cycles, and planning sessions.
  
  
**What You'll Do**
**Planning & Forecasting**

* Own the integrated operating model — maintain a multi-schedule three-statement model with scenario testing, clear source mappings, and documented logic changes.
* Build the annual budget & planning cycle across revenue, OpEx, headcount, and cash alongside department heads.
* Manage headcount and compensation planning, keeping forecasts reconciled with HRIS census and approved compensation structures.
* Model revenue dynamics including platform fees vs. media pass-through, take rates, gross vs. net revenue, and AdTech unit economics.
* Design the planning rhythm — establish budget-vs-actuals reviews, spend approval workflows, and monthly business reviews.

**Reporting & Close**

* Support the monthly close alongside Accounting by preparing accruals, reviewing actuals, and analyzing variances.
* Deliver monthly reporting packages with variance analysis against budget, forecast, and prior periods.
* Maintain system reconciliations, including NetSuite-to-Looker bridges with fully documented variance drivers.
* Analyze profitability across products, business lines, customers, and channels.
* Track core KPIs including ARR, NRR, gross/logo retention, cohort profitability, CAC payback, and gross margins.
* Prepare stakeholder materials for Board, lender, and investor presentations, including debt covenant calculations.

**Controls & Data Integrity**

* Ensure data accuracy by tying out deliverables against approved models and control totals before distribution.
* Validate source data from NetSuite, Looker, Salesforce, and HR systems before model ingestion.
* Maintain version control and document all formula, logic, and mapping updates across shared tools.

**Business Partnering**

* Partner with department leaders across the organization to evaluate spend and stress-test assumptions.
* Manage tech & AI economics — forecast cloud spend, build cost attribution tags, and track AI/LLM unit economics.

**Systems, Automation & Data**

* Streamline FP&A workflows by optimizing ERP and planning systems to reduce manual processes.
* Standardize metrics & reporting in collaboration with BI, Systems, and Accounting.
* Document financial processes to ensure scalability, audit readiness, and continuity.

**Who You Are**

* 4–6 years of experience in FP&A, strategic finance, corporate finance, investment banking, or consulting.
* Bachelor's degree in Finance, Economics, Accounting, or a quantitative field.
* Advanced financial modeling experience building integrated 3-statement models from scratch.
* Strong control discipline with a proven track record of error-free, board-grade deliverables.
 [...] * Experience with Board and lender reporting or debt covenant tracking.
* Big 4, investment banking, or consulting training.
* Hands-on experience with ERPs/planning tools (NetSuite, Adaptive, Pigment, Anaplan).
**You'd Be a Great Fit If**
* Detail-oriented with high accuracy standards and a strong self-check discipline.
* Cross-functional influencer who can partner across teams to drive financial discipline.
* Tech & AI-forward mindset to leverage modern tools for speed and deeper analysis.
* Resourceful problem solver comfortable navigating ambiguity and shifting priorities.
**What Success Looks Like**
**In your first 90 days**
* Master the business model, own core reporting deliverables, and establish model audit controls.
**By the end of your first 6 months**
* Deliver reliable operating models, timely close reporting, and automated FP&A workflows.

About Rockefeller Capital Management:

Rockefeller Capital Management was established in 2018 as a leading independent financial advisory services firm. Originally founded in 1882 as the family office of John D. Rockefeller, the Firm has evolved to offer strategic advice to ultra- and high-net-worth individuals and families, institutions, and corporations from offices in 37 markets throughout the United States, as well as an office in London. The Firm oversees $236 billion in client assets as of September 30, 2026.

Position:

As a core member of the Marketing team, the Senior Events Associate will play an integral role in bringing Rockefeller’s distinctive brand and client experience to life through high-touch events for clients, prospects, advisors, and other key stakeholders.

The individual will lead the strategy, planning, production, and execution of complex in-person, virtual, and hybrid events. They will partner closely with senior leaders, Marketing colleagues, and business stakeholders across the organization to translate business objectives into thoughtfully designed experiences and flawlessly executed programs.

The ideal candidate is a strategic, highly organized event professional with experience in financial services, strong business and financial acumen, exceptional attention to detail, and the confidence to work directly with senior stakeholders. This is an individual-contributor role requiring someone who can independently lead programs, influence cross-functional partners, manage external resources, and remain hands-on throughout planning and execution.

Responsibilities:

* Lead the end-to-end planning and execution of client, prospect, advisor, and internal-focused events, translating business objectives into clear event strategies, deliverables, and measures of success.
* Manage creative, logistical, and technical elements, including program format, attendee journey, registration, food and beverage, branding, curation of event signage and collateral, audiovisual production, show flow, speaker logistics, security, transportation, and onsite execution.
* Develop, manage, and reconcile event budgets and related expenses, balancing premium experiences with fiscal discipline.
* Build trusted relationships with senior leaders and cross-functional partners, advising stakeholders on event objectives, audiences, formats, content, and the overall attendee experience.
* Partner with Communications and other internal teams to ensure consistent branding and coordinated pre-event, onsite, post-event, and social media communications.
* Manage short- and long-term plans, timelines, dependencies, and competing priorities across multiple programs. Proactively identify risks and develop solutions and contingency plans.
* Source and manage venues, production partners, hospitality providers, and other vendors, including contract negotiations, scopes of work, deliverables, performance, and expense oversight.
* Define event metrics and analyze participation, engagement, attendee feedback, ROI, and spend. Apply insights and lessons learned to strengthen future programs.
* Monitor developments across events, hospitality, technology, wealth management, and financial services, incorporating relevant trends and insights into program ideation and planning.
* Develop and continuously improve event templates, run of show documents, and self-service resources that strengthen consistency, efficiency, and best practices across the organization.

Qualifications:

* 5–7 years of experience in corporate event planning, experiential marketing, or a similar function, with financial services experience required.
* Demonstrated success managing complex, high-touch client, prospect, and executive events from strategy through onsite execution and post-event measurement.
* Working knowledge of wealth management, asset management, private banking, investment management, or a related business is highly valued.
* Proven ability to work effectively with senior executives and influence cross-functional stakeholders.
* Demonstrated experience managing event budgets, vendor contracts, production partners, and complex logistics.
* Excellent judgment, discretion, problem-solving skills, and attention to detail.
* Ability to operate independently in a fast-paced, quick-response environment while maintaining a highly collaborative approach.
* Ability to travel approximately 15%.
Skills:
* Proficiency with CVENT, including registration, attendee management, communications, reporting, and event-management workflows.
* Proficiency with Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Copilot, with the ability to responsibly leverage AI and productivity tools to improve planning, communications, research, analysis, and operational efficiency.
* Exceptional project-management and organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and programs simultaneously.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills; comfortable presenting and working directly with internal and external stakeholders.
Compensation Range:
The anticipated base salary range for this role is $115,000 to $130,000. Base salary for the role will depend on several factors, including a candidate’s qualifications, skills, competencies, and experience, and may fall outside of the range shown. In addition, this role may be eligible for a discretionary bonus. Rockefeller Capital Management offers a comprehensive benefit package including health coverage, vacation time, paid leave, retirement plan, and more. Visit careers.rockco.com to learn more about additional opportunities and benefits offerings.

The Tunnel to Towers Foundation is committed to eradicating homelessness amongst our veterans.

The Construction team for the Homeless Veteran Program (HVP) leads the planning, design, and development of veteran housing communities that provide safe, high-quality, and supportive living environments for America’s veterans. Our work directly supports the mission of eradicating veteran homelessness by creating dignified housing solutions and purpose-built communities that enable veterans to rebuild their lives while strengthening the neighborhoods in which they live.

The Foundation is seeking an experienced Senior Associate Director of Construction to support and assist the Director of Construction, HVP and Vice President of Construction, HVP in each phase of commercial construction and renovation of new acquisitions (commercial and hospitality construction). * Strong written and oral communication skills.
* Excellent multitasking skills.
* Ability to work under pressure with minimal supervision.
* Excellent problem-solving skills.

This is a full-time, on-site position based at the Foundation’s office. Employees are required to work in the office during their regularly scheduled business hours. Remote and hybrid work arrangements are not available for this position.

**A Note From the Founder**
Citizen builds with agents now, and that changes what a finance leader does. The close, the forecast, the board package, the variance analysis: producing these is no longer the job. The judgment behind them is.
  
  
Consumer subscription revenue is growing, the enterprise business is working and ready to scale, and the product that made us the #1 safety app in America is going global. Each of those is a financial question as much as a product one: what to price, what to fund, what to stop. I need one leader who owns the whole financial model, keeps the books and board materials ready, leads our investor and board relationships alongside me, and gives me a straight answer when the numbers say something different from the plan. That person works next to me, every day.
  
  
**The Role**
Citizen is the #1 safety app in the U.S. Every day, thousands of videos are captured live at the scene of real incidents and distributed in real time to people in every major American city. No other consumer product has this. It is a live network, a newsroom, and a safety tool at once, and it is growing. Our mission is simple: Protect the World.
  
  
The VP of Finance & Business Operations owns Citizen's financial and operating engine end to end: planning and forecasting, accounting and the close, audit, tax, treasury and cash, fundraising and investor reporting, board management, the company KPIs and the instrumentation behind them, strategic planning and OKRs, vendor negotiation, strategic partnerships, and the data room that keeps the company ready for its next financing or its exit. You report to the Founder and serve as his partner on capital, the board, and strategy. You sit on the leadership team and work most closely with the leaders of engineering and technology, product, applied AI, growth, and enterprise sales. You manage the finance team: a Finance & Business Operations Manager, to be hired in New York, and an Accounting Manager.
  
  
You will not build a large finance organization. The production work of finance is carried by agents you design and operate, with your team holding the controls and the signatures. One leader with the right systems and the right judgment now carries what a finance organization of ten carried three years ago. This seat is built on that premise.
  
  
This is the seat for a Series B to C stage finance leader who has run the function before, or been the clear number two in a larger one, and wants to own it outright.

Citizen built the public safety category and became the #1 safety app in the country. The next chapter is a product people open every day, a subscription business that funds it, an enterprise business that is already working and ready to scale, and Citizen around the world. Every one of those bets has a financial decision underneath it, and the company is about to make several at once. This seat is for one executive who sees the whole model, knows which growth lever is real, keeps the books and the board ready, and can run the capital process alongside the Founder. Until recently that person needed a department. Now they need agents, rigor, and the nerve to decide.

Every role at Citizen is two things: the craft, and the operation of AI to multiply it.
  
  
You are a finance leader first. Judgment about what a dollar should do and what it should not. The discipline of a clean close, an audit-ready set of books, and a forecast the board can rely on. The standing to run a solo conversation with a board director or an investor and come back with the company's position intact.
  
  
You will work alongside colleagues who are not people. Eve is our engineering agent; she lives in the codebase and ships. You build the business case, pressure-test it with the leaders who will run it, and bring the Founder a recommendation with the model open. Accountabilities:
The Financial Analyst will support corporate FP&A activities by delivering accurate financial analysis, actionable insights, and reliable reporting while helping improve financial processes and systems. Key responsibilities include:
- 
 Perform financial statement, expense, and variance analyses to identify performance drivers, investigate discrepancies, and communicate actionable insights to management.
- 
 Support corporate budgeting, forecasting, and financial planning activities, including the preparation of financial models and reporting packages.
- 
 Assist in preparing quarterly Board of Directors and executive presentations, including consolidated forecasts, segment reporting, and financial analyses.
- 
 Analyze company-wide headcount, spending, bookings, revenue, and capital expenditures to support business planning and decision-making.
- 
 Administer and enhance global financial consolidation and reporting systems, including SAP BPC, through troubleshooting, data validation, and user support.
- 
 Identify and implement process improvements using automation, data analytics, and technology to improve reporting accuracy and operational efficiency.
- 
 Independently manage assigned financial processes, reporting deliverables, and recurring deadlines while identifying opportunities for continuous improvement.
- 
 Collaborate with Corporate, Product Line, and Operations Finance teams to coordinate reporting, resolve discrepancies, and strengthen cross-functional processes.
- 
 Support monthly and quarterly financial close activities, including forecast submissions, journal entries, and reporting requirements.
- 
 Conduct ad hoc financial analyses and contribute to strategic initiatives, including potential merger integration and financial systems projects.
 Requirements :
 The ideal candidate combines a solid accounting foundation with strong financial analysis capabilities, technical aptitude, and a proactive approach to problem-solving. They should be comfortable managing responsibilities independently while collaborating with stakeholders across a global organization. Required qualifications include:
- 
 Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field, with at least 5 years of relevant experience in public accounting, FP&A, corporate finance, or financial reporting; or a master's degree in a related field with at least 3 years of relevant experience.
- 
 CPA designation preferred.
- 
 Strong understanding of financial statements, accounting principles, forecasting, and financial analysis.
- 
 Advanced Microsoft Excel skills, including financial modeling, pivot tables, and complex formulas.
- 
 Experience preparing presentations and reporting materials using Microsoft PowerPoint.
- 
 Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities, with the capacity to investigate discrepancies, identify trends, and translate complex financial information into meaningful insights.
- 
 Technical aptitude and interest in financial systems, data management, and reporting automation.
- 
 Experience with SAP BPC, SAP ECC, or comparable ERP and financial consolidation systems is highly desirable.
- 
 Familiarity with Power Query, Power BI, Alteryx, Sigma, SQL, or similar analytical tools is an advantage.
- 
 Experience working with ERP, financial consolidation, planning, or reporting platforms.
- 
 Demonstrated ownership of financial processes and the ability to coordinate cross-functional activities.
- 
 Self-directed and proactive approach, with the ability to take initiative, solve problems independently, and drive improvements beyond assigned responsibilities.
- 
 Strong organizational and communication skills, including the ability to manage competing priorities and work effectively with stakeholders across different functions.
 Benefits :
- 
 Annual salary ranging from $82,000 to $105,000, depending on location, experience, and other job-related factors.
- 
 Eligibility for a bonus opportunity.
- 
 Medical, dental, and vision insurance.
- 
 401(k) retirement plan with company matching.
- 
 Paid holidays, vacation, and sick time.
- 
 Flexible Spending Accounts (FSAs).
- 
 Commuter benefits.
- 
 Life and accident insurance.
- 
 Disability insurance.
- 
 Tuition reimbursement.
- 
 Employee Assistance Program (EAP).
- 
 Identity theft remediation services.
- 
 Emergency travel assistance.
- 
 Fully remote work flexibility.

description:
ABOUT US

Ediphi https://www.ediphi.com/ offers the most comprehensive cloud-based estimating and preconstruction solution on the market. Our goal is to reduce the time spent in preconstruction, enabling projects to break ground more quickly and estimators to feel more confident in their work.


We started when Michael Navarro, a former estimator at Suffolk, knew there was a better way than relying on spreadsheets. He began creating a solution built by estimators, for estimators. He teamed up with Dustin DeVan, founder of BuildingConnected (acquired by Autodesk for $275 million https://adsknews.autodesk.com/en/pressrelease/autodesk-to-acquire-buildingconnected/), to launch Ediphi in 2023. With a $12M Series A https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/ediphi-announces-12-million-series-a-funding-from-norwest-venture-partners-to-expand-team-and-enhance-cloud-based-estimating-solution-for-preconstruction-302096090.html?tc=eml_cleartime round led by Norwest Venture Partners and with ongoing participation from Suffolk Technologies, Ediphi continues to grow as a SaaS offering for General Contractors around the country.




ABOUT THIS ROLE

Collections are one of the most closely tracked parts of our business. You will work directly with our CEO and leadership team on where things stand and surface issues well before anyone notices. Accounts receivable at Ediphi is currently spread across several team members. Follow-up happens between other responsibilities, so we are hiring one person to own this function end to end.



You will be responsible for knowing the status of every dollar we are owed. That means what has been invoiced, what has been paid, what is sitting in a customer's AP portal, and what needs a call today. When a deal closes, you ensure it gets billed correctly and on time. When a payment is late, you will be the person following up.



We typically carry ten to twenty open invoices at a time, so this is not high-volume billing work. You will know every account by name, and once the process is established, you will have time for work beyond AR. The next area of responsibility is financial analysis, which includes maintaining our financial model, reviewing it with our accounting firm, and supporting the CEO on planning. WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own AR end to end. Create and send new and renewal invoices accurately and on time in QuickBooks, and keep billing records clean.

WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - Accuracy with numbers and records. Errors in billing data cost us money and credibility with customers.
 - Follow-through without reminders. You track your own commitments and flag risks early.
 - Strong AI and spreadsheet skills. You can build and maintain a tracker other people can read and use.
 - Discretion and judgment. You will handle sensitive financial information and work with limited oversight.
 - Comfort with ambiguity. This function is being built as you go, and there will not be an established playbook for every situation.
NICE TO HAVE

title: Strategic Finance
description:
THE GAP NO ONE HAS FILLED

Every complex system in America has a profession whose job it is to be your trusted guide. You have a lawyer for legal. An accountant for taxes. A financial advisor for your money. Healthcare, a trillion-dollar industry that's arguably the most complex and touches every single family, leaves us on our own.

99% of care happens when someone steps outside the four walls of a doctor's office. Hera is creating a new profession in healthcare to fill that gap: the Hero, a dedicated senior care expert for your family. Our Heroes educate, coordinate, and advocate for the most vulnerable population in the healthcare system. We’re covered by insurance, so we can serve every family in America.




BUILDING THE MOST TRUSTED INTERFACE OF HEALTHCARE

We are in the business of trust.

We're designing for the most emotionally charged moments of our customers' lives; the bar isn't just delight, it's trust. Hera's brand promise is simple: care worthy of our parents. This promise is our moat.

It's what physicians refer to, families buy, what Heroes deliver, and what the product must unlock and enforce at every touchpoint.




OUR PRODUCT CHALLENGE 

The bottleneck isn't demand, it's supply. There aren't enough experts to serve every family who needs us. To scale to all of America, we have to unbundle expertise from the human so that anyone who can foster human connection can become a Hero. 

The problem is that this expertise is tribal knowledge. One social worker knows how to expedite Medicaid in New York, another knows which home-visiting PT families actually love. It's trapped in people's heads.  

To solve this,  our platform captures every interaction and turns it into compounding intelligence that makes every user smarter. Think Waymo: expert humans do the driving today, and every mile they log trains the system so that tomorrow, anyone — even with zero healthcare background — can perform like a 20-year veteran. The hard part is building a system that knows what to trust, what's gone stale, what's local versus universal, and how to surface the right insight at the right moment. Get it right and you've scaled healthcare expertise beyond the lucky few who know the right person.

We wrote more on why and how we are building this technology here. https://hellohera.notion.site/what-endures-when-execution-is-free




OUR FOUNDING TEAM

We've raised $34M from Accel and Bain Capital Ventures and 10x'd revenue over the last 6 months organically through close partnerships with Weill Cornell, NYU Langone, UCSF, USC, and Mount Sinai. Chief of Geriatrics at Weill Cornell and Director of Geriatrics at NYU Langone have joined us as clinical advisors. CFO of Mount Sinai has invested in us. 
The customer feedback is the most positive our team has seen in our careers. Along the way, we threw an art show for an 88 year old artist that went viral https://ny1.com/nyc/all-boroughs/news/2026/02/19/88-year-old-brooklyn-painter-sells-art-for-the-first-time and a talent show https://www.instagram.com/reel/DZi3YmESZ6Q/?igsh=MTR3cjg4ZmJvb2NyZQ%3D%3D where every act is over 65.
You’ll build Hera alongside co-founders Jenny https://www.linkedin.com/in/jennydlee/, Myles https://www.linkedin.com/in/mylesnovick/ & Connie https://www.linkedin.com/in/jingyi-connie-kang/ and a team from Palantir and Headway. We are in person in NYC. Read our story and watch our launch video here https://hellohera.com/about.







JOIN US TO BUILD OUR STRATEGIC FINANCE FUNCTION

At most companies, finance is a reporting function: close the books, build the budget, explain the variance. This role is different; it is not an FP&A role. At Hera, you're in the room for every big investment we make, and you own the math behind it. Every Hero we hire, every market we open, every payer we contract with and every program we bill under is a bet with a cost and a return that either compounds or doesn’t. You’ll turn those bets into numbers we trust, then go out and move the numbers. 
You’ll bring the analytical rigor of a seasoned financier and the ethos of a strong operator: surgical execution, relentless truth seeking and an obsession with greatness. You'll work through hard tradeoffs in the business and then go make it happen.
PROBLEMS YOU’LL OWN
 - Unit economics. Both sides of it. On the Hero side: what it costs to recruit, train, ramp and retain a Hero, how many families a Hero can serve before the 20% starts falling behind, and where our platform bends that curve. On the family side: what it costs to find and onboard a family, how much value we deliver to families, and how long they stay with us. You’ll build the model that ties the two together, then work with growth teams to move its inputs.

 - The company operating model. Own the equation that connects growth inputs (patient referrals, Hero capacity, product levers) to revenue and margin. Set targets with each team and run the cadence that holds us to them.
 - Capital strategy. Cash planning, board and investor materials, fundraising prep. Treat capital as a scarce resource, and point it at the highest-leverage bets.
You’ll own the plan and the model, but you won’t spend your week reconciling accounts or writing variance commentary. If you love figuring out why a number is what it is and then fixing it, we'd love to chat.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for an Operations Finance Manager to be the finance partner to the people who run our manufacturing network. WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Support strategic decisions. Build the analysis behind manufacturing equipment purchases, manufacturing footprint decisions, and insource vs. outsource evaluations — and have a point of view on the answer, not just the model.


QUALIFICATIONS

description:
As our Regional Manager of Operations, Mid-West , you'll play an important role in supporting and growing a diverse portfolio of emergency, specialty, and urgent care hospitals.
 You'll work directly with Practice Managers, Hospital Administrators, Medical Directors, and veterinary partners to strengthen daily operations, improve financial performance, develop hospital leaders, and create exceptional experiences for clients, patients, and referring veterinarians.
 This role combines hands-on operational leadership with regional business oversight. You'll spend time in hospitals, build relationships with teams, understand the challenges they face, and help develop practical solutions that improve performance.
 You'll also partner closely with our Regional Vice President and central support teams to implement operational initiatives, support hospital growth, and identify opportunities across the region.
 This isn't a role for someone who wants to manage hospitals from behind a spreadsheet. We're looking for someone who enjoys being in the field, coaching leaders, solving problems, and helping teams turn great ideas into measurable results.
 Most importantly, we're looking for a leader who understands that successful hospitals are built through strong relationships, engaged teams, sound business decisions, and consistent execution.
 What You'll Do 
 Lead Regional Hospital Operations 
- Provide operational oversight and support for multiple specialty, emergency, and urgent care hospitals throughout the Mid-West region.
- Partner with hospital leadership to improve daily workflows, staffing efficiency, patient access, and overall operational performance.
- Establish consistent operational expectations while respecting each hospital's unique culture, clinical services, and business needs.
- Identify operational challenges early and work collaboratively with hospital teams to implement sustainable solutions.
- Maintain a strong field presence through regular hospital visits, leadership meetings, and ongoing communication.
 Drive Financial & Business Performance 
- Take ownership of regional financial performance, including revenue growth, EBITDA, labor management, expense control, and profitability.
- Partner with hospital leaders to develop and execute budgets, forecasts, and financial improvement plans.
- Monitor key performance indicators, including revenue, transactions, average transaction charges, labor costs, staffing productivity, and client experience metrics.
- Identify opportunities to improve hospital efficiency, manage expenses, and support sustainable growth.
- Translate financial data into clear, actionable priorities for hospital leadership teams.
 Develop & Empower Hospital Leaders 
- Coach and mentor Practice Managers, Hospital Administrators, and department leaders to strengthen their leadership and business management skills.
- Establish clear expectations, accountability, and consistent follow-through across hospital teams.
- Support leadership development, succession planning, and employee engagement initiatives.
- Partner with Human Resources and Talent Acquisition on recruiting, retention, performance management, and staffing strategies.
- Help hospital leaders navigate challenging conversations, organizational changes, and complex operational situations.
 Support Emergency, Specialty & Urgent Care Operations 
- Understand and support the different staffing, scheduling, workflow, and financial models across emergency, specialty, and urgent care hospitals.
- Partner with medical leadership to improve veterinarian scheduling, clinical support staffing, patient flow, and operational efficiency.
- Identify opportunities to improve appointment availability, service utilization, and access to veterinary care.
- Support hospital teams in managing the operational demands of extended hours, overnight services, and fluctuating caseloads.
- Collaborate with medical leaders to remove operational barriers while respecting clinical decision-making and medical autonomy.
 [...]  Required Experience & Qualifications 
- 5+ years of progressive veterinary hospital operations experience , preferably within emergency, specialty, urgent care, or a combination of these environments.
- 2+ years of multisite leadership experience or comparable senior-level management experience within a large, complex veterinary hospital.
- Demonstrated success improving hospital financial performance, operational efficiency, and team engagement.
- Strong financial acumen, including P&L management, budgeting, labor management, forecasting, and expense control.
- Experience coaching and developing Practice Managers, Hospital Administrators, or other hospital leaders.
- Understanding of veterinary hospital staffing models, veterinarian productivity, clinical workflows, and operational performance metrics.
- Ability to build strong relationships with veterinary professionals, medical leadership, and hospital partners.
- Excellent communication, problem-solving, organizational, and leadership skills.
- Ability to manage competing priorities across multiple hospitals and geographic markets.
- Bachelor's degree in business, healthcare administration, veterinary management, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
- Willingness and ability to travel extensively throughout the assigned region.
 Even Better If You Bring 
- 7+ years of veterinary hospital leadership experience, particularly within specialty, emergency, or urgent care.
- Previous experience as a Regional Manager, Area Manager, Hospital Administrator, Director of Operations, or senior veterinary practice leader.
- Experience overseeing multiple hospitals, large multidisciplinary teams, or 24-hour emergency operations.
- Experience supporting hospital integrations, new hospital openings, service expansions, or operational turnarounds.

description:
Location: Remote

Job Type: Full-Time Independent Contractor (~40 hours/week)

 

We are partnering with a U.S.-based technology company building advanced AI systems focused on financial modeling and decision-making.

 

Important Experience Requirement:

Minimum 2 years of full-time, paid finance experience after graduation. Internships, training programs and course projects do not count. This role is not suitable for students or recent graduates.

 


ABOUT THE OPPORTUNITY

The goal of this project is to train AI to think like real financial professionals: how models are built from scratch, how assumptions are structured, and how credit and debt decisions are made using financial models.

 

This is a hands-on Excel modeling role where you will build detailed credit and debt models from a blank spreadsheet and explain your logic. We prioritize candidates who can build full models end-to-end and explain why a model works, rather than just producing summary dashboards or tweaking templates.

 

We evaluate two distinct technical tracks under this posting:

 - Credit: 3-statement borrower models, cash flow-based lending, debt sizing, covenant modeling, loan structuring, and downside cases. (If your experience is in leveraged finance, direct lending, or project finance, your background fits our Credit area).
   
    

 - Debt: Bond pricing, fixed income analysis, and portfolio construction.
   
    


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Build dynamic financial models from scratch in Excel across credit underwriting or debt valuation scenarios.
   
    

 - Structure assumptions, drivers, and logic while linking full cash flow, debt schedule, and downside flows.
   
    

 - Model and link 3-statement borrower financials, amortization schedules, payment-in-kind (PIK) interest, dynamic cash sweeps, DSCR, and debt covenants (Credit track).
   
    

 - Structure bond pricing, yield curves, and fixed income portfolio construction models from the ground up (Debt track).
   
    

 - Review, debug, and improve model accuracy by identifying incorrect assumptions, broken logic, and structural risks.
   
    

 - Clearly explain financial logic, decision-making, and why a model works in structured English.
   
    


MUST-HAVE REQUIREMENTS

 - 2+ years of full-time, paid finance experience post-graduation with heavy modeling exposure in Credit, Private Credit, Direct Lending, Leveraged Finance, Project Finance, Fixed Income, or Bond Portfolio Management. Candidates from Investment Banking or Corporate Finance are considered only with top-tier backgrounds.
   
    

 - Real-World Model Building: The models you describe must have been built in your job, on real deals or real lending decisions. Models from training courses or case studies do not count.
   
    

 - Proven ability to build full financial models from a blank spreadsheet in Excel without using pre-built templates, plug-ins, or AI tools.
   
    

 - Track-Specific Technical Execution:
   
   - Credit Track: Hands-on experience structuring 3-statement borrower models, debt sizing, DSCR and covenants, amortization schedules, PIK interest, cash sweeps, and downside cases.
     
      
   
   - Debt Track: Direct experience with bond pricing, fixed income analysis, and portfolio construction.
     
      

 - High attention to detail, model accuracy, and strong professional communication skills in English to clearly articulate financial logic.
   
    

 - Ability to complete an independent ~3-hour technical modeling take-home assessment in Excel.
   
    

 - Availability to dedicate full-time hours (~40 hours per week) on an ongoing independent contractor basis.
   
    


THIS ROLE IS / THIS ROLE IS NOT

 - This role IS: Hands-on model building from a blank workbook, creating benchmark datasets, auditing logic, and articulating institutional financial reasoning.
   
    

 - This role is NOT: An internal corporate finance, FP&A, or deal-structuring role; it does not involve loan administration, retail collections, or client presentations.
   
    


NOT A FIT IF

 - You rely on pre-formatted templates, third-party calculators, or add-ins to build your models.
   
    

 - Your modeling background comes primarily from academic courses, financial modeling bootcamps, or case studies rather than professional employment.
   
    

 - You are currently seeking a part-time role or cannot commit to ~40 hours per week.
   
    


WHY JOIN?

 - Full-time independent contractor role with full flexibility: 100% remote, asynchronous workflow where contractors set their own working hours.
   
    

 - Opportunity to work at the forefront of AI financial reasoning and institutional benchmarking.
   
    


HOW TO APPLY

ABOUT IRIS

IRIS Software Group is one of the UK's largest privately held software companies, trusted by 100,000+ businesses, schools and accountancy firms to keep their operations running. Our software pays 1 in 6 UK employees, supports over 12,000 schools, and is relied on by 91 of the top 100 UK accountancy firms.

We're a Great Place to Work® certified employer, recognised for our commitment to well-being, inclusion and development - and we're growing fast.

At IRIS, we build software that helps organisations manage the people processes they rely on every day. Within our Workforce Management business, Swipeclock provides technology that helps employers and their partners manage areas including timekeeping, scheduling, attendance and workforce operations.

We’re looking for a Technical & Scripting Support Team Lead who can combine people leadership with genuinely hands-on technical problem solving.

Experience in time and attendance technology is essential, but you don't necessarily need a SaaS background. We're equally interested in candidates from workforce management or payroll service providers who understand how time and labour processes impact payroll.

You’ll guide our Technical and Scripting Support Team while remaining close to the work: troubleshooting complex customer issues, reviewing and writing scripts, coordinating software defect investigations, and helping customers and partners get the best from our solutions.

Working Location & Hours

We're ideally looking for candidates based in the Central or Mountain time zones, although Eastern and Pacific time zones can also be considered.

Our working hours are:

 - Eastern: 11am–8pm

 - Central: 10am–7pm

 - Mountain: 9am–6pm

 - Pacific: 8am–5pm

 

🧾 Why This Role Matters

This is much more than a traditional support leadership role.

You’ll be the first point of escalation when the team encounters particularly complex or high-impact issues and will help turn customer requirements into practical technical solutions. You’ll also coach analysts, improve the quality of support cases, and work closely with our Development, Product, Customer Success and Professional Services teams.

Your influence will stretch from an individual customer issue through to improvements in our products and support operation.

 

👥 About the Team You'll Join

You’ll lead specialists supporting Swipeclock, our Workforce Management technology business. The product portfolio includes WorkforceHub, TimeWorksPlus, ApplicantStack and TimeSimplicity, covering areas such as workforce management, time and attendance, recruitment and scheduling.

You’ll work with both customers and Channel Partners, external businesses that provide Swipeclock solutions and services to their own customers.

 

📊 What You'll Be Doing

 - Lead the team day to day, coordinating workloads, priorities and technical direction while coaching analysts through feedback, case reviews and hands-on problem solving.

 - Act as the first point of contact for complex customer escalations and help ensure the team meets agreed service levels (SLAs), the standards used to measure how quickly and effectively support is delivered.

 - Scope, prioritise, test and deliver custom scripting requests, including writing and reviewing code using Swipeclock’s proprietary scripting language.

 - Troubleshoot complex issues across software, time-clock hardware, APIs, networking and third-party integrations.

 - Improve case quality within Salesforce Service Cloud, ensuring problems, investigation steps, solutions and follow-up actions are clearly documented.

 - Lead bug triage, the process of investigating, documenting and prioritising potential software defects before working with Development to progress them.

 - Partner with Product, Development, Customer Success and Professional Services to tackle recurring issues and improve customer outcomes.

 - Use Salesforce reports and dashboards to provide visibility of service levels, case backlog, escalations, quality and customer outcomes.
 [...]  - Participate in the team’s holiday and weekend on-call rotation.
🔎 What We’re Looking For
You’ll bring:
 - Experience in time and attendance or time and labour technology is essential, whether gained within a software company, workforce management provider or a business such as ADP.
 - At least 2 years’ experience in customer service or technical support, with the ability to investigate and resolve technical issues.
 - Experience leading, mentoring or providing senior-level guidance within a technical support environment.
 - An understanding of how timekeeping, attendance and labour management processes affect payroll. In-depth payroll or HR expertise is not required.
 - Working knowledge of Salesforce CRM or Salesforce Service Cloud.
 - Strong analytical and troubleshooting skills, with the confidence to work through complex technical and customer problems.
 - Clear written and verbal communication skills and the ability to work effectively with customers, partners and technical colleagues.
 - The ability to balance competing priorities while remaining hands-on.
 - Two years of college-level study in Computer Science, IT or a related discipline, or equivalent education and experience.
Programming or scripting experience would be particularly valuable, as would knowledge of C#, APIs, automation, software integrations, networking or clock hardware. Experience with SaaS platforms, scheduling, leave/accrual tracking or payroll integrations would also be beneficial.
You don’t need previous Swipeclock experience. Familiarity with Swipeclock products or another Workforce Management platform would be an advantage.

Most fund finance seats are a person doing the work. This one is a person deciding what the work should be, then building the agents that do it.

Equi runs alternative strategies through several layers of onshore and offshore vehicles. That structure is what lets us bring hard-to-access strategies to advisors and family offices, and it makes the accounting, money movement and reporting more demanding than a ten-person firm suggests. We need one senior leader to own all of it, and to make it run on systems rather than on anyone's attention.

About Equi

Equi gives investors the tools to own their financial future. We bring institutional-quality alternative strategies, in hedge funds and private credit, that are hard to get access to, to wealth advisors, family offices and institutions. We build and manage multi-strategy funds and white-labeled funds for some of the best independent multi-family offices and advisory firms in the country, pairing Silicon Valley tech with Wall St expertise.

Our growth is accelerating rapidly. We just launched the largest client in our history, have several more signed or close, and are targeting a multiple of today's assets. We're about ten people, so every hire here shapes a function rather than inheriting one. We hire builders and team players that aren't afraid of taking a high degree of ownership.

The role

You'll own finance and fund operations for the fund complex and the management company, reporting to the CEO. That means the NAV cycle and the reconciliation behind it; capital calls, distributions, redemptions and onboarding; every wire and the controls around it; budget, treasury, audit and tax; investor reporting; and the setup of every new vehicle.

We own our books. You'll build and run an internal shadow NAV for every vehicle, one we're 100% confident in, and reconcile it against our administrator every cycle. When the numbers disagree, you decide the firm's position, and you hold our administrator, auditor, counsel and banks to a standard. Partners should be checking our work, not telling us what our numbers are.

When something recurring is manual, you build the thing that removes it instead of absorbing it or hiring for it. These agents touch investor money, so the bar is production, not demo: each one is checked against an independent source, has evals that catch a regression when a prompt or model changes, and hands off to a person instead of failing silently. If you can't say how you'd know an agent got something wrong, it doesn't go live.

What success looks like in year one

 - We run our own shadow NAV on every vehicle and trust it fully, every close reconciles it against the administrator, and nothing reaches an investor without your sign-off

 - Agents handle statement intake, reconciliation, exception flagging and the first pass of reporting, each with checks that prove it right

 - Every wire runs on documented controls with dual approval, and an auditor could walk through them today

 - Our own books: an internal shadow NAV on every vehicle, reconciled against the administrator each cycle, with your final sign-off

 - Fund operations: capital calls, distributions, redemptions, subscriptions and investor onboarding

 - Money movement: cash across operating and fund accounts, and approval authority on every wire

 - Corporate finance: fund expense budget and allocation, burn and runway, board reporting, payroll and benefits

 - Audit, tax and compliance: counterpart to the auditor and tax preparer, working with our compliance partner

 - Launches: the financial setup of each new vehicle, with outside counsel on structure and documents

 - Investor service: reporting that goes out on time, and fast, honest answers to investors and advisers
 - The provider network: administrator, auditor, tax preparer, counsel, prime brokers and banks, held to a written standard
Who you are

You've built or run a shadow NAV, and you find the error in a draft NAV before anyone else does.
 - A builder: you've shipped agents and automations, not just used AI. You can tell us what you built in the last six months, what it changed, where it broke, and how you proved it right before trusting it with real numbers.

 - Hands-on: you've worked somewhere small enough that you did the work yourself. If the close always belonged to a team two levels down, this isn't the seat.

Nice to have: layered multi-vehicle structures, offshore vehicles and their audit cycle, ERISA and plan-asset monitoring, or a CPA or legal background (or equivalent depth earned another way).
How we work
Team-first, flat and direct. Ideas win on merit, people argue a position and change their mind when the evidence says so, and nobody stays narrowly in lane when there's an adjacent fire. description:
Over the last 20 years, Ares’ success has been driven by our people and our culture. Today, our team is guided by our core values – Collaborative, Responsible, Entrepreneurial, Self-Aware, Trustworthy – and our purpose to be a catalyst for shared prosperity and a better future. Through our recruitment, career development and employee-focused programming, we are committed to fostering a welcoming and inclusive work environment where high-performance talent of diverse backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives can build careers within this exciting and growing industry. 
 Job Description 
 Job Description 
 Company Overview 
 Ares Management Corporation (“Ares” or the “Firm”) is a publicly traded, leading global alternative asset manager with approximately $572 billion of assets under management ("AUM") and approximately 4,100 employees. We seek to deliver attractive returns across each of our strategies and believe our investment groups are market leaders based on assets under management and investment performance. Our distinct but complementary teams have the ability to invest across a company’s capital structure, from senior debt to common equity. The Firm was built upon the fundamental principle that each group benefits from being part of the broader platform. We believe the synergies from this multi-asset strategy provides our professionals with insights into industry trends, access to significant deal flow and the ability to assess relative value.  
 Since our inception in 1997, we have adhered to a disciplined investment philosophy that focuses on delivering compelling risk-adjusted investment returns throughout market cycles. We believe our growth in becoming one of the largest alternative asset managers is a testament to our experienced management team, our focus on performance and our high-quality investor base, which includes large pension funds, university endowments, sovereign wealth funds, banks and insurance companies. 
 Roles & Responsibilities 
 Ares is currently searching for a highly motivated, diligent teammate to join as a full time Associate in our Ares Insurance Solutions (“AIS”) Strategy Group. AIS is our dedicated, in-house team that seeks to provide asset management, origination, risk analytics, capital, and M&A services to insurance clients globally. The team currently manages ~$25Bn of AUM across a broadly diversified asset portfolio and is the investment manager, capital solutions provider and corporate development partner to Aspida, a leading U.S. life and annuity insurance and reinsurance company. 
 The AIS Strategy Group consists of investment professionals working directly with the heads of AIS and leaders across Ares to source, evaluate and implement upon our highest priority growth initiatives. Projects led by this group include management company acquisitions, minority investments, strategic partnerships, global expansion, and business development. 
 The group seeks to strategically deploy Ares, Aspida, and third-party capital in accretive opportunities that enhance our current capabilities and / or expand our product offerings. The Associate will provide support for the sourcing, evaluation and execution of potential new pivotal initiatives for Ares Management and AIS. Key role responsibilities include: 
- Performing detailed financial and market analysis that forms the basis for decisions on investments of the firm 
- Preparing complex excel financial models 
- Screening new investment opportunities 
- Preparing investment committee memos and board presentations 
- Analyzing investment performance including maintaining and updating financial models as well as keeping track of relevant current market activities 
- Assisting in investment closings and diligence 
- Supporting strategic projects for new business development initiatives across the AIS and the firm 
- Additional duties include providing direct support as deemed necessary by senior management 
 Requirements 
- Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Mathematics or related field (MBA or CFA a plus) 
- 7+ years of relevant investment banking, consulting, or principal investing preferably with focus on asset management / financial services or insurance 
- Impeccable integrity and trustworthiness. The AIS Corporate Strategy Group is often required to work with sensitive information and a candidate must be willing and able to handle this information appropriately 
- Self-motivated with the ability to set priorities, multitask, and monitor own workload to meet deadlines 
- High level of attention to detail 
- Strong analytical skills and the ability to work well with limited supervision 
- Private equity caliber drive and ability to work effectively in a collegial, fast moving, demanding, and dynamic environment 
- Creative problem solver 
- Strong interpersonal and communication skills 
- Highly proficient in Excel, PowerPoint and Word

Principal, Ares Insurance Solutions

That person is moving on to bigger things, and we need someone to step into that seat, formalize what works, and keep roughly 200 price changes a month running accurately, on time, and grounded in real conversations with the General Managers who run our buildings.

You start the morning scanning the pricing dashboard and notice a suite at 1411 Broadway that hasn't sold in weeks, while the identical suite next door is occupied at full list price. You ask about tour volume, application quality, and whether the floor plans still fit what people are searching for. You leave the call with a plan, and the GM leaves it feeling like someone actually looked at their building, not just their numbers.



In the afternoon, you work through the week's renewal batch, running each one against the pricing logic the team uses to decide what gets pushed through and what needs a second look. You flag one segment where occupancy has slipped two months running, log it for deeper review, and jot down a note on the decision tree so the next person doesn't have to relearn it from scratch.

To learn more, visit www.industriousoffice.com/careers http://www.industriousoffice.com/careers.



About the Role

Industrious signs new landlord partnerships every year, and the number is growing as our business development team expands. Before any of those deals move forward, someone has to check that it holds together: that the assumptions are sound, that the start date, budgets, rent, pricing, and returns all track, and that the figures from design and construction have carried through correctly. As a Real Estate Associate on our Real Estate Transactions team that will be your job!



You will underwrite assigned deals in Excel, explain what drives their returns, and flag where a deal is tight, whether on pricing, occupancy, or CapEx. Our business development colleagues make the call on whether a deal goes ahead, and your analysis is what they rely on to make it well. You will work with Design, Construction, Finance, and other teams to make sure every number is right, supporting several business development colleagues as deal flow shifts.



Our approach to underwriting is different from a traditional real estate shop, and we will teach it to you. In your first few months you will get close review and clear guidance while you learn how we work. You will also join at a good time: the team is growing, new roles are being added, and we are underwriting a new product, so there is real room to learn, ask questions, and grow with us.



Success here means accurate work. The team trusts your numbers, your flags are clear, and any mistake you make happens once, not twice.



What Might Your Day Look Like

Your morning starts with a new deal from one of our business development colleagues. You go through the model piece by piece: the start date, the budget, the rent and revenue share assumptions, the cash flows, the IRR, and the margin the location is expected to earn per rentable square foot. The returns look fine at first, but pricing is tighter than it seems, so you note it clearly with the number that would need to change.



Late morning, updated figures arrive from Design and Construction. You check that they have flowed into the model correctly. One CapEx figure does not match the construction budget, so you confirm the right number with the construction team before it goes any further.



In the afternoon, you walk your business development colleague through the deal: what the returns look like, where the risk sits, and which assumptions matter most. They decide what happens next. Then priorities shift, and another colleague needs support on a deal heading to Investment Committee, so you move over and check that every figure in the review material ties back to the underwriting.



Before you wrap up, you update your trackers and checklists so the team knows where every deal you are supporting stands.



What You Will Own

 - Underwrite assigned deals in Excel, checking every assumption and making sure each component, from start date and budgets to pricing and IRR, tracks.
 - Explain each deal's returns clearly, including IRR, cash flows, P&L, and margin, so business development can make an informed decision.
 - Flag where a deal is tight, on pricing, occupancy, CapEx, OpEx, rent, or revenue share, and where it may need more support.
 - Make sure figures from Design, Construction, and Finance carry through accurately into the deal.
 - Support deal reviews and Investment Committee materials with numbers that hold up to scrutiny.
 - Support several business development colleagues across their deal flow, moving between priorities as needs change.
 - Keep the trackers and checklists that help the team stay accurate as deal volume grows.

 A GLOBAL FIRM WITH A DIVERSE & INCLUSIVE CULTURE  
 As the Global Asset Management business of Prudential, we’re always looking for ways to improve financial services. We’re passionate about making a meaningful impact - touching the lives of millions and solving financial challenges in an ever-changing world.  We also believe talent is key to achieving our vision and are intentional about building a culture on respect and collaboration. When you join PGIM, you’ll unlock a motivating and impactful career – all while growing your skills and advancing your profession at one of the world’s leading global asset managers! If you’re not afraid to think differently and challenge the status quo, come and be a part of a dedicated team that’s investing in your future by shaping tomorrow today.  At PGIM, You Can!  
 What you will do  
 The Portfolio Analysis Group (PAG) partners closely with investment teams to provide the analytics and insights that support portfolio construction, risk monitoring, performance analysis, and investment decision-making. 
 Our PAG Analyst Program is a three-year rotational program designed to provide broad exposure across asset classes, investment strategies, and portfolio management teams. Analysts complete one-year rotations across PAG and select partner teams, developing a strong foundation in portfolio analytics while gaining firsthand experience across the investment process. 
 Core rotations may include General Account, Investment Grade, High Yield, Emerging Markets, US/Global Rates & Hedge Fund, Structured Products, and Multi-Sector. Satellite rotations may include CLO Structuring, Structured Products Research, and Investment Risk Management. 
 This incoming Analyst will begin the program aligned to our Structured Products / Asset-Based Finance (ABF) team , where they will work closely with Portfolio Managers and other investment partners to analyze portfolio positioning and performance, monitor risk and client objectives, and deliver actionable insights that support day-to-day portfolio management. 
 This position follows a hybrid work model, with working 3 days in the Newark, NJ office and 2 days remote. 
 What you can expect  
- Analyze portfolio positioning relative to benchmarks, client objectives, risk parameters, and investment goals, identifying changes in exposures and opportunities to improve portfolio alignment. 
- Produce portfolio analytics and performance attribution to help explain investment results and inform portfolio management decisions. 
- Incorporate client guidelines, investment objectives, and risk tolerances into portfolio monitoring, scenario analysis, and portfolio management workflows. 
- Partner with Portfolio Managers, Traders, Risk Managers, Quantitative teams, Credit Research, Client Advisory, technology partners, and senior PAG team members. 
- Support timely market, portfolio, and client analyses while improving recurring reports, analytical tools, and repeatable processes. 
 What you will bring  
- Bachelor’s degree and 2+  years of relevant experience in investment management, financial services, portfolio or risk analytics, research, or a related analytical field. 
- Proficiency with Excel and familiarity with investment and data analytics tools such as Bloomberg, Aladdin, SQL, and Python preferred. 
- Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to turn complex analysis into clear, actionable insights.  
- A collaborative mindset and ability to work effectively across investment, risk, research, and technology teams. 
 What will set you apart  
- Strong analytical skills, intellectual curiosity, and a proactive approach to problem solving. 
- Ability to manage multiple priorities and deliver accurate, high-quality work in a fast-paced investment environment. 
- Exposure to coding best practices, including documentation, version control, testing, peer review, and writing maintainable code. 
- Pursuit of the CFA designation or an MBA is a plu s.

title: Senior Strategy & Decision Analyst
description:
THE ROLE 
 The Senior Strategy & Decision Analyst exists to ensure the Group's most consequential decisions are made with demonstrable Decision Quality (DQ) - that by the time the Board, CEO, or a business unit commits, the decision meets the standard of the six DQ elements: an appropriate frame, creative and doable alternatives, meaningful and reliable information, clear values and trade-offs, sound reasoning, and commitment to action. Given the close interdependence between strategy and decision quality, this role also carries primary responsibility for elaborating the Group's and Business Unit’s cascading strategies, working directly and continuously with the respective leaders - so that strategy and the decisions that implement it are developed together rather than handed off at the end. The role acts as the organization's honest broker: neutral on which alternative wins, uncompromising on the quality of the process that selects it, and on embedding risk-based, optionality-oriented thinking into decisions and their execution design from the outset. 
 KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: 
 Strategy elaboration 
- Hold regular meetings and workshops with leaders across the organization to elaborate and implement their cascading strategies, help identify their key growth initiatives and strategic issues, and collect bottom-up input for Group strategy iteration. 
- Assist the Board and CEO with Group strategy definition and contribute to the negotiation of key agreements. 
- Help operations translate key growth initiatives and strategic issues into budget inputs, in collaboration with Finance. 
- Shape strategy continuously based on what is happening on the ground and in interactions with stakeholders, and vice versa - ensuring strategy work and decision support reinforce each other rather than operating as separate tracks. 
 Decision framing and structuring 
- Work with the executive team to frame the organization's most consequential decisions: define the decision hierarchy (policy, strategic, tactical), clarify what is being decided, by whom, and against which values, before analysis begins. 
- Structure complex decision situations into clear decision elements - decisions, risks/uncertainties, and values - using influence diagrams, decision hierarchies, and strategy tables. 
- Ensure a genuinely creative and distinct set of alternatives is developed for every major decision, including hybrid strategies, and explicitly preserve optionality in how decisions are executed. 
 Decision analysis and evaluation 
- Lead the quantitative evaluation of strategic alternatives: stochastic analysis for financial and operating and project development decisions, probabilistic financial modelling, Monte Carlo simulation, decision trees, tornado and sensitivity analysis, and real options valuation for staging, deferral, and expansion flexibility. 
- Quantify uncertainty rigorously - elicit calibrated probability assessments from technical and commercial experts, and actively counter cognitive and motivational biases in those inputs. 
- Apply value-of-information and value-of-control analysis to direct study, piloting, and de-risking spend toward the uncertainties that actually matter to the decision. 
- Make value trade-offs explicit - NPV versus risk, growth versus resilience, short-term cash versus strategic positioning - so decision-makers choose with clear eyes rather than by implicit assumption.

SENIOR DATA ANALYST, PRODUCT ANALYTICS
 Current is a leading consumer fintech platform transforming financial access for everyday Americans with over 6 million members. We provide access to financial solutions that seamlessly work together to solve the needs of our members and enable all Americans to build better financial futures. Based in NYC, our results-driven environment drives us to build better products, grow faster and empower everyone on our team to have an impact on our business and mission to improve financial outcomes.
 ABOUT THE ROLE
 We are looking for a Senior Data Analyst, Product Analytics to play a central role in how our product and business teams make decisions. You will be embedded with teams across areas such as banking, user journey and experience, liquidity, and value-added services, owning the analytics agenda for your area from question to recommendation. This is a high-ownership role: you will lead experimentation, drive deep-dive and root-cause analyses, build business cases, and help your partners set strategic roadmaps. You are equally comfortable writing complex SQL and presenting a clear point of view to leadership, and you raise the analytical bar for the people around you.
 RESPONSIBILITIES
- Own the product analytics agenda for your embedded area, partnering with product, engineering, finance, and business leaders to scope, prioritize, and deliver high-impact analyses.
- Lead the design, execution, and interpretation of experiments, including success metrics, power and sample sizing, statistical inference, and learning briefs.
- Conduct deep-dive and root-cause analyses on trends, funnels, retention, and engagement, turning ambiguous problems into clear business opportunities.
- Build business cases that size opportunities, quantify impact, and inform investment and roadmap decisions.
- Help department leaders define success metrics and strategic roadmaps grounded in data.
- Provide clear, actionable insight to stakeholders on business performance, customer behavior, and metric trends, and present findings and recommendations to leadership.
- Build and maintain dashboards, reports, and Looker explores that track KPIs across product, finance, and operations.
- Partner with analytics engineers and data engineers to improve data models, definitions, and reliability, and to validate outputs before they reach stakeholders.
- Use AI tools to improve efficiency in analysis, insight generation, and reporting, and share best practices with the team.
- Mentor and support other analysts, contributing to team standards for analysis design, experimentation, and storytelling.
 ABOUT YOU
- Bachelor's degree in a quantitative field such as Statistics, Economics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
- 5+ years in a data analytics role, with at least 3 years in product analytics, where you owned multiple concurrent workstreams and operated with a high degree of autonomy.
- 2-3 years in a consumer-facing fintech, digital banking, payments, or lending environment (or similar B2C setting), working with transactional data, product metrics, and customer behavior at scale.
- Advanced SQL in a cloud data warehouse environment (Snowflake, BigQuery, or Redshift), including window functions, CTEs, and complex joins.
- Python experience for data analysis, automation, and statistical work.
- Strong expertise in experimentation, including A/B/n testing, significance testing, and statistical inference.
- Proven track record of taking analytical projects from scoping through to delivery, with ownership over outcomes, not just outputs.
- Experience building dashboards and reports in Looker or comparable BI tools.
- Strong written and verbal communication, and the ability to present findings and recommendations to non-technical stakeholders and leadership.
- A proven ability to use data to change minds and drive decisions.
 NICE TO HAVE
- Direct experience in D2C or consumer fintech, including banking, liquidity, or value-added services.
- Experience building business cases and contributing to roadmaps or strategic planning.
- Hands-on experience with dbt or comparable transformation tools, and familiarity with dimensional modeling.
- Experience using AI tools to improve analytics efficiency and insight generation.
- Experience mentoring analysts or leading cross-functional workstreams, even informally.
- Familiarity with unit economics concepts such as ARPU, contribution profit, and cohort LTV.
 This role has a base salary range of $150,000 - $200,000. Compensation is determined based on experience, skill level, and qualifications, which are assessed during the interview process. Current offers a competitive total rewards package which includes base salary, equity, and comprehensive benefits.
 BENEFITS
- Competitive salary
- Meaningful equity in the form of stock options
- 401(k) plan
- Discretionary performance bonus program
- Biannual performance reviews
- Medical, Dental and Vision premiums covered at 100% for you and your dependents
- Flexible time off and paid holidays
- Generous parental leave policy
- Commuter benefits
- Fitness benefits
- Healthcare and Dependent care FSA benefit
- Employee Assistance Programs focused on mental health
- Healthcare advocacy program for all employees
- Access to mental health apps
- Team building activities
- Our modern NYC based office with open floor plan, stocked kitchen, and catered lunches

About the Role
 The Sort Capacity Manager owns network-wide capacity de-risking for the Sort organization. This role builds and maintains the constraint model that defines what “de-risked capacity” means across every 1P and 3P facility — dock door availability, floor/pallet-position space, max throughput, and optimal labor and automation. 
 About the Team 
- Own the network constraint model — Model site capacity against its underlying constraints: dock door availability (inbound/outbound truck cadence by hour, translated from Mx forecast), floor/pallet-position space (inbound-to-outbound hourly volume vs. staging capacity), max throughput (automation vs. manual sortation rate, package profile mix, cross-dock vs. sort), and optimal labor hours required to hit max output.
- Govern spoke capacity data — Drive spoke capacity maintenance in the sort app, ensuring product reflects current facility configuration, and hold cross-functional partners accountable when it doesn't.
- Own zip-to-facility strategy — Own zip code-to-facility mapping and re-optimization as volume and rates shift, balancing service-level and cost trade-offs.
- Own device and consumable readiness — Forecast scanners, bins, and gaylords against site growth to avoid reactive procurement; own the readiness cadence end to end.
- Scope hub-to-spoke routing opportunities — Build the business case for hub-sort-to-spoke direct routing and bring recommendations forward to Network Design and Real Estate.
- Close forecasting product gaps — Identify where forecasting tools fail to capture capacity reality and drive the fix with Data/Product partners.
- Own Mx launch — Own Mx launch end to end, including CET allocation by merchant priority, negotiating trade-offs across competing merchant demands.
 You're excited about this opportunity because you will… 
- 3-6-12 month runway visibility ahead of any projected capacity constraint.
- Site launch recommendations delivered proactively, not reactively.

- Strategic model ownership — You've built and owned a capacity, forecasting, or network constraint model that became a standing input to planning — not a one-off analysis.
- Independent judgment — You can independently judge where the real bottleneck is across a large, multi-site network, without a pre-scoped problem statement.
- Cross-functional negotiation — You've negotiated trade-off recommendations with senior, cross-functional stakeholders (e.g., Network Design, Real Estate, Finance) and influenced capital-adjacent decisions.
- Physical operations fluency — You understand physical warehouse operations deeply enough to translate dock, floor, throughput, and labor constraints into a single model.
- Experience — 7+ years in supply chain, network strategy, or operations, with direct experience owning capacity planning or site launch strategy at scale.
- Executive communication — You communicate trade-offs and risk clearly and concisely to senior leadership, and you know what to escalate versus resolve independently.

 Extend is revolutionizing the post-purchase experience for retailers and their customers by providing merchants with AI-driven solutions that enhance customer satisfaction and drive revenue growth. Our comprehensive platform offers automated customer service handling, seamless returns/exchange management, end-to-end automated fulfillment, and product protection and shipping protection alongside Extend's best-in-class fraud detection. By integrating leading-edge technology with exceptional customer service, Extend empowers businesses to build trust and loyalty among consumers while reducing costs and increasing profits.
Today, Extend works with more than 1,000 leading merchant partners across industries, including fashion/apparel, cosmetics, furniture, jewelry, consumer electronics, auto parts, sports and fitness, and much more. Extend is backed by some of the most prominent technology investors in the industry, and our headquarters is in downtown San Francisco.

 You'll join our centralized Risk, Analytics & Data Science (RAD) team as a Senior Manager, serving as the leader in the Finance Analytics function and help build and scale up the team. You'll be accountable not just for your own forecasts and models being right, but for the team's methodology and financial data being sound.
