title: Revenue Operations Lead
description:
ABOUT TRIBE AI

Tribe AI helps companies build and ship real AI solutions. We bring together a network of top AI practitioners with a delivery team that turns AI strategy into production systems for our clients. Our go-to-market team is growing fast, and we need someone to make our revenue engine run on data, not intuition.


ABOUT THE ROLE

We're looking for our first person to own revenue operations. You'll be the only person in the function and work directly with Head of GTM. This is a hands-on role: you'll do the analysis yourself, and your analysis will shape decisions.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

Own forecast operations

 - Build and run the forecast and bookings roll-up end to end.

 - Add the judgment on top of the numbers. Flag when a rep is behind, sandbagging or overcommitted, or when a deal is slipping, and raise it before the forecast call rather than in it.

 - Get to one bookings number the whole room trusts.

Build our core GTM metrics and reporting

 - Stand up the metrics we're missing today: time to close, days in stage, loss rate and partner funnel. Partners feed our sales pipeline, so this covers more than direct sales.

 - Refresh them on a regular cadence so that a sales-metrics question gets a real answer the same day.

 - Where the data underneath isn't clean, fix it. Set and enforce stage definitions and pipeline hygiene.

Run the weekly GTM operating rhythm

 - Own prep for the weekly GTM meeting: the data pull, the analysis and choosing which topics need attention.

Own deal desk and commissions

 - Run commissions for 60+ sellers on an ongoing basis.

 - Own our commissions platform (Spiff), which is being implemented now, and the comp plan templates behind it.

 - Administer next year's sales comp plans, covering plan mechanics, accelerators, draws and clawbacks, and partner with GTM leadership on plan design.

Build AI-powered tools for the GTM team

 - Build Claude skills and automations that improve how the GTM team works, such as proposal building and project plans.

 - Build the back-end infrastructure behind our GTM operations with AI, rather than managing it by hand.

Support finance and planning

 - Answer ad-hoc GTM and sales-metrics questions from our strategic finance team, and supply the forecast they use for business planning.

 - Support territory planning and GTM org design as needs come up.

What this role isn't: delivery or project metrics, margins, accounting, or financial planning. Those sit with our delivery and strategic finance teams. You'll be the source of GTM truth that feeds them.


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE IN YOUR FIRST 90 DAYS

 - GTM leadership walks into forecast calls having read your analysis instead of building one, and anomalies are flagged in advance.

 - Time to close, days in stage, loss rate and partner funnel exist, refresh on a cadence and are trusted.

 - Commissions run through Spiff, not Excel.

 - Next year's comp plans are drafted and ready to administer.

 - Weekly GTM call prep is fully yours.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

Must-haves

 - Minimum of 6 years of experience in the field

 - You're AI-native. You build real infrastructure with AI (Claude, agents, skills, automations), not just use it to write emails. An engineering background is a strong signal.

 - Experience in Revenue Operations, Sales Operations, GTM Operations or GTM Systems inside a B2B revenue organization. Depth matters more than years: we need someone who understands go-to-market, not a generalist analyst.

 - Hands-on sales commissions experience at scale. You've run comp for a sizable sales team, not just reported on it, and you understand plan mechanics, draws, accelerators and clawbacks.

 - You've built forecasts and pipeline metrics yourself, end to end, often from imperfect data.

 - Strong GTM judgment. You've sat in real pipeline reviews and can explain why a rep's forecast looks wrong, not just that it differs from plan.

 - A real preference for hands-on work. You want to be the person building the analysis, not directing an analyst, and you're comfortable being a team of one.

 - Strong opinions on stage definitions and forecast hygiene, and experience enforcing them with sellers.

Nice-to-haves

 - Experience at a services, consulting or professional-services company. SOW-based bookings behave differently from recurring subscription revenue.

 - Experience implementing or administering a commissions platform (Spiff, CaptivateIQ, Xactly or similar).

 - Deal desk experience: pricing approvals, deal structuring, contract review with sales.

 - Partner or channel funnel analytics.

 - A background in software engineering or Salesforce consulting.


WHY JOIN

 - Real impact from day one. You're building the function, not maintaining someone else's.

 - Direct access to leadership. You'll work side by side with the GTM leader, and your analysis drives the conversation.

 - Breadth. Forecasting, analytics, deal desk and comp all sit in one seat, at a company at the center of applied AI.

title: Demand Planning Manager
description:
The Role   
 The Demand Planning Manager is responsible for leading the demand planning process across “ markets ” in our cannabis portfolio, translating commercial strategy, market trends, historical performance, inventory positions, and operational inputs into a clear, accurate , and actionable demand plan.   
 This role serves as the primary link between Commercial, Marketing, Supply Planning, and Operations, ensuring the organization is aligned on what products are needed, where they are needed, when they are needed, and in what quantities. The Demand Planning Manager will establish and continuously improve demand planning processes, forecasting methodologies, and analytical capabilities across a complex, multi-state cannabis business. This includes managing demand at the appropriate level of detail across markets, brands, product categories, SKUs, strains/flavors, and channels while balancing forecast accuracy with the speed and volatility inherent in the cannabis industry.   
 The ideal candidate is highly analytical, commercially minded, operationally oriented, and comfortable making decisions in an environment where historical data alone is not sufficient to predict future demand.   
 This is a remote position. The candidate will work Eastern or Central Time business hours.  
 Responsibilities   
- Own the demand planning process and maintain the rolling demand forecast across all applicable markets, product categories, brands, and SKUs. 
- Develop and maintain a rolling 12-month demand plan, with increased detail and accountability across the near-term planning horizon. 
- Translate historical sales, POS trends, inventory, pricing, promotions, seasonality, market growth, new product launches, product lifecycle changes, and commercial assumptions into a robust demand forecast. 
- Develop appropriate forecasting methodologies by product/category based on demand characteristics, lifecycle, market maturity, and data availability. 
- Facilitate demand review meetings and drive resolution of significant gaps between the commercial forecast, statistical forecast, and operating plan. 
- Identify meaningful changes in demand trends and proactively communicate risks, opportunities, and recommended actions to appropriate teams  
- Manage new product forecasting, including demand assumptions, launch curves, cannibalization, and product ramp-up/ramp-down. 
- Identify demand/supply gaps and quantify the potential revenue, service, and inventory implications. 
- Establish appropriate methodologies for managing promotions, price changes, market expansions, product discontinuations, and other demand-impacting events 
- Manage exit plans for products we want to wind down, playing a role in both identifying products for divestiture and managing the off ramp process 
- Collaborate effectively with supply planners and lead plans for hand off demand plans to supply chain planners 
- Use AI to enhance and improve processes and functions  
 Qualifications    
- Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain, Business, Finance, Economics, Analytics, or related field. 
- 7+ years of experience in demand planning, forecasting, supply chain planning, S&OP, or related discipline. 
- Experience managing forecasts across multiple products, locations, markets, or channels. 
- Strong analytical and quantitative skills with the ability to translate data into business decisions. 
- Demonstrated experience with forecasting methodologies, inventory planning, and S&OP / IBP processes. 
- Advanced Excel skills and experience working with ERP, planning, and business intelligence systems. 
- Strong communication and cross-functional collaboration skills. 
- Ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, highly dynamic environment with incomplete or changing information. 
- Experience in the cannabis, CPG, consumer products, retail, food & beverage, pharmaceutical, or other highly regulated industry. 
- Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management, Business, Operations, Finance, Engineering, or a related field. 
- Experience and comfortability using AI. 
 Additional Requirements   
- Must pass  any and all  required background checks    
- Must be and remain compliant with all legal or company regulations for working in the industry    
- Must be a minimum of 21 years of age

 The pay range is competitive and based on experience, qualifications, and/or location of the role. Positions may be eligible for a discretionary annual incentive program driven by organization and individual performance.

 $110,000 — $130,000 USD

About Intellistack

At Intellistack, we're committed to revolutionizing the way organizations collect information, automate workflows, and create seamless digital experiences.

Founded with the belief that work should be simplified, Intellistack has grown into a leading provider of powerful, no-code productivity solutions that help teams do more with less. With intuitive solutions that put power in the hands of everyday users, we make it easier to build, automate, and optimize processes at scale.

Who We Are
At Intellistack, we don’t do status quo. We move fast, think deep, and build what’s next—powered by people, supercharged by AI.

We’re a team of builders: curious, driven, and relentless about solving the real problem. Around here, feedback is fuel, clarity wins, and change is the default setting. If you’re hungry to grow and ready to leave a dent, you’ll fit right in.


WHO YOU ARE

We are seeking a Business Analyst to lead analysis for Formstack’s digital self-serve SaaS business, with a focus on SMB customers. You will connect marketing, website, product, billing, and customer data to understand how customers discover Formstack, purchase, adopt the product, stay, and grow. Your work will help teams prioritize changes that improve customer outcomes and ARR.

This is a hands-on business analytics and decision-support role. You will define useful metrics, investigate performance, build trusted reporting, and evaluate the impact of growth and retention programs. You will also provide account insights and measure handoffs that support the broader Formstack sales motion. The core responsibility remains digital self-serve analytics; this role does not own campaign execution or revenue operations.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

Understand acquisition and conversion

 - Build and maintain a scorecard covering qualified traffic, acquisition spend, signup, purchase, activation, new customers, and new ARR.

 - Analyze performance by channel, campaign, customer segment, and cohort, including conversion, acquisition cost, customer quality, and payback.

 - Identify friction in the website, pricing, signup, checkout, and early product experience. Evaluate whether changes improve conversion and downstream retention.

Improve Retention and Expansion

 - Track customer and ARR retention by cohort, product, contract term, health, and segment. Explain churn, contraction, reactivation, pricing, and expansion through a consistent ARR bridge.

 - Combine product use, support, billing, and engagement signals to identify customers at risk and opportunities to improve adoption. Measure the results of retention programs against appropriate comparison groups.

 - Identify, size opportunities and segments for seat growth, upgrades, cross-sell and upsell. Measure conversion, expansion ARR, and subsequent customer health.

Turn data into decisions

 - Use SQL and Databricks to develop reliable customer-level analyses, partnering with data teams on definitions, data quality, and reusable datasets.

 - Build dashboards and forecasts that show performance across the self-serve customer journey and explain changes to business stakeholders.

 - Evaluate experiments, automated journeys, and agentic programs using measures such as reach, completion, escalation, conversion, retained ARR, and expansion ARR.

 - Surface qualified digital intent signals for sales teams and measure the outcomes of sales-assisted handoffs especially related to upsell motion.


WHAT YOU BRING

 - 4+ years of experience in business intelligence, growth analytics, product analytics, or a related analytical role; experience in digital self-serve or SMB SaaS is strongly preferred.

 - Strong SQL skills and experience analyzing customer-level data in a cloud data platform such as Databricks.

 - Experience with digital funnels, product event data, cohorts, dashboards, and experiment measurement.

 - Working knowledge of SaaS measures including ARR, GRR, NRR, churn, expansion, customer acquisition cost, and lifetime value.

 - Ability to explain findings in clear business terms.


HELPFUL EXPERIENCE

 - Pendo or a similar product analytics platform; Zuora, Salesforce, web analytics, and a BI tool.

 - Churn or expansion propensity analysis, pricing measurement, or evaluation of automated customer journeys.


SALARY RANGE

$90,000 - $100k base salary + 5% variable bonus based on company and individual performance.

ABOUT CROSBY

Crosby is built on a simple conviction: a great legal system is the watermark of a great society — and the best legal work comes from combining human expertise with the right technology, not replacing one with the other.

Crosby is the first AI-native law firm, helping ambitious companies like Cursor, Ramp, and Cognition sign commercial contracts faster.

Legal work is both art and science, and we're mapping the frontier between the two — codifying what can be systematized, amplifying human judgment where it matters most. That's why the right way to bring AI into law isn't to sell software and walk away. It's to own the outcome together: higher-quality work, delivered faster. We build proprietary tools and human-in-the-loop workflows that change what's possible for corporate legal teams.

Crosby was founded by Ryan (Stanford Law, Cooley, startup GC) and John (Penn, first 15 engineers at Ramp).  Help us transform one of society's most important industries.


About the role

Build the systems behind Crosby’s next stage of growth.

You’ll own the processes, data, and tools that help us turn demand into lasting client relationships. Working closely with the COO and leaders across Sales, Growth, Finance, and Legal Operations, you’ll bring clarity to how we acquire clients, convert pilots, grow accounts, and plan for what comes next.

Our business requires understanding both what clients commit to and how they actually use Crosby. You’ll connect pipeline, commercial terms, client activity, and revenue so we can make better decisions about where to invest and how to scale.

This is a hands-on role with broad ownership. You should be equally comfortable building a forecast, configuring a CRM workflow, and helping a sales leader understand why conversion changed.

What you’ll do

 - Own our commercial systems: Build and maintain the CRM, integrations, and workflows our teams rely on. Establish clear account ownership, pipeline stages, lead routing, and data standards—and make the systems easy to use.

 - Make revenue performance clear: Build reporting that connects pipeline, pilot conversion, signed commitments, client usage, retention, and expansion. Partner with Finance to keep bookings, billed revenue, and collections clearly defined and reconciled.

 - Run forecasting and pipeline reviews: Establish a consistent cadence with Sales and Finance. Pressure-test assumptions, identify stalled deals and risks, and turn the forecast into specific actions.

 - Help scale the sales team: Build capacity and hiring models, account assignments, quota recommendations, and ramp reporting. Partner with leadership and Finance on compensation plans and accurate commission calculations.

 - Improve conversion across the client journey: Find where prospects and clients get stuck—from initial inquiry through pilot, onboarding, and expansion. Work with the relevant teams to fix those gaps and measure whether the changes work.

 - Connect the sale to delivery: Make sure pricing, commitments, and client expectations transfer cleanly into onboarding and billing. Give Legal Operations visibility into expected demand so we can plan capacity as we grow.

 - Automate repetitive work: Use AI, integrations, and practical tooling to reduce manual updates, improve data quality, and give the team more time with clients. Own adoption and reliability after launch.

Who you are

 - You’ve built before: You have 5–8 years of experience in Revenue Operations, Sales Operations, or a closely related function, including meaningful ownership at a fast-growing B2B company.

 - You get into the systems yourself: You’ve configured a CRM, built workflows and integrations, and resolved the data issues behind unreliable reporting. Experience with Attio, Salesforce, or HubSpot is relevant.

 - You’re analytically strong: You can build a forecast, capacity model, or cohort analysis yourself and explain what it means. You’re excellent in spreadsheets; SQL and experience with BI tools are a plus.
 - You understand commercial nuance: You can distinguish a signed commitment from realized revenue and translate pilots, variable usage, and expansion into useful reporting and planning.
 - You make teams more effective: You earn trust with salespeople, introduce processes people actually follow, and hold a high standard for accuracy and accountability.
 - You have strong judgment: You know when to build something durable and when a simple solution will get the team moving. You can prioritize a broad mandate without waiting for a detailed roadmap.
 - You’re curious and resourceful: You actively use AI and automation in your work, learn unfamiliar tools quickly, and take responsibility for seeing projects through.
What success looks like
Leadership has a clear, trusted view of pipeline and revenue. Salespeople spend less time on administrative work. Pilots, onboarding, and expansion have clear owners and measurable outcomes. Hiring and capacity decisions are grounded in data. The systems you build help Crosby grow while keeping the team fast.

We're looking for a strategic financial leader to join our team as Senior Manager of Financial Planning & Analysis. In this role, you'll be at the heart of how AbsenceSoft plans for the future – partnering with executive leaders, driving smarter forecasting, and translating financial data into insights that shape our growth. If you're a collaborative, detail-oriented finance professional who thrives in a fast-moving environment, we'd love to meet you. 
 WHAT YOU'LL DO 
- Lead the development and execution of annual budgets, quarterly forecasts, and long-range financial plans. 
- Manage, mentor, and develop the FP&A team, fostering alignment with organizational goals and professional growth. 
- Provide financial insights and analysis to support executive and board-level decision-making, including direct reporting to the CFO. 
- Partner with Sales and Marketing to forecast ARR, and collaborate with department leaders on performance insights and variance analysis. 
- Develop and enhance financial models to evaluate business scenarios, strategic initiatives, investments, and partnerships. 
- Drive process improvements and automation to increase efficiency in financial reporting, while supporting month-end and quarter-end close processes with Accounting. 
- Participate in a highly compliant environment and assist in maintaining company security and compliance controls 
- Other duties as assigned 
 WHAT YOU'LL BRING 
- Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field. 
- 7–10 years of progressive finance experience, including at least 2 years in a leadership role, and experience within a relevant SaaS enterprise environment. 
- Strong background in FP&A, budgeting, forecasting, and financial modeling, with advanced Excel skills. 
- If local - an enthusiasm for a hybrid work environment, with approximately 2 days per week of in-office presence in our downtown Denver location. If fully remote, an ability to manage efficient operations in a remote work environment. 
- Excellent communication and presentation skills, with the ability to influence stakeholders at all levels. 
- High attention to detail, strong business acumen, and demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities under tight deadlines. 
- Proficiency in financial systems such as Cube, Pigment, and NetSuite. 
 Why join us 
 At AbsenceSoft, we LEAD with our values: 
 Lead with Innovation - We create meaningful change through intelligence, focus and passion.   We embrace curiosity, data, and insight to shape the future of our industry. Always innovating, learning and evolving. 
 Elevate Every Voice - Every perspective matters. We listen, learn, and build a culture where diversity of thought and experience drives better solutions and smarter decisions.  
 Achieve Together - The customer fuels everything we do. We share knowledge, collaborate, celebrate wins, and face challenges as one team because success is always a collective achievement. 
 Drive Outcome - Every action we take delivers measurable value to our teams, our customers, and the employees they support. Accountability is non-negotiable. We honor our commitments, take responsibility for results, and see every success and setback as a chance to grow stronger. 
 We offer: 
- Impact that matters. You’ll do work that shapes the future of the modern workplace 
- Flexibility and trust. We’re remote-first and results driven. You’ll have the freedom and flexibility to do your best work, wherever you do it best. 
- Growth and development. We believe the best work happens when people are growing. You’ll have access to learning resources, leadership programs, and real opportunities to take on new challenges and expand your impact.   
- Competitive rewards. We offer comprehensive benefits, a performance-based bonus program, and equity opportunities – because when we grow, you should too. 
- Time for life. Recharge and reconnect with flexible time off, paid holidays, and flexible leave programs designed to support every season of life. 
- Belonging and balance. We’re building an inclusive culture where every voice is valued, collaboration is celebrated, and success is shared. 
 We’re committed to building a team as diverse as the customers we serve. If your experience doesn’t align perfectly with every qualification, we still encourage you to apply you might be exactly what we’re looking for. If this sounds like a fit, apply today, we’d love to meet you! 
 Final compensation is determined based on a candidate's relevant experience, skills, education, and geographic location. This position is also eligible for annual bonus. 
 At AbsenceSoft, we’re transforming the employee experience. Our secure, intuitive technology helps employers bring humanity, certainty, and efficiency to some of the most complex moments in the workplace. Built by HR professionals for HR professionals, we’re proud of where we’ve been and even more excited about where we’re going.

title: Data Science Associate | Involved Media | NYC
description:
About the role 
 The Data Science Associate is an entry-level role on the Analytics team. The supports recurring client deliverables, automates repeatable analytics work, and helps build a structured, queryable database of campaign results. The Associate also uses knowledge of Client data and business to help Data Scientists scope and build forecasting and predictive models. 
 What you'll do 
 Analytics & Reporting 
- Support recurring client deliverables, including weekly refreshes, post-log processing, station weighting, and monthly and quarterly reporting. 
- Maintain campaign pacing data and predictive budget tracking models; flag performance dips and efficiency changes to the team. 
- Build and maintain reporting in Power BI. 
- Summarize campaign results in clear, plain-language performance summaries for internal teams and clients. 
 Forecasting & Predictive Modeling 
- Build and maintain forecasting models for client business results such as orders, enrollments, applications and donations, including budget scenarios and in-flight reforecasts. 
- Develop predictive models that estimate the impact of changes in media spend and mix, and identify performance shifts early. 
- Validate model accuracy against actual results, and document methods and assumptions. 
- Support Data Scientists by briefing on modeling, analysis and data requests. 
 Automation & Data Quality 
- Document recurring workflows step by step and identify tasks that can be scripted, scheduled or automated with AI tools. 
- Replace manual checks with automated alerts and processes. 
- Establish QA and validation checks to identify tracking anomalies and reporting discrepancies. 
- Maintain documentation of client data sources, ownership, update frequency, tracking links and taxonomy mappings. 
 Results Database & Projects 
- Help design and populate a structured, queryable database of campaign results across clients, including spend, delivery, response, outcomes and campaign context. 
- Ensure the team's analyses are captured in the results database. 
- Scope longer-term needs such as models, pipeline fixes or new dashboards; brief the Data Science and BI teams and track projects to completion. 
 Qualifications 
- Bachelor's or master's degree in Statistics, Applied Mathematics, Mathematics, Data Science, Computer Science, Operations Research, Econometrics or quantitative Economics, Biostatistics, Physics, or Industrial and Systems Engineering; master's degree preferred. 
- Coursework in probability and mathematical statistics, linear algebra, regression and statistical modeling, and programming; database or data-engineering coursework a plus. 
- Proficiency in SQL and Python or R. 
- Working knowledge of applied statistics and modeling, including regression, time-series forecasting, predictive modeling and experimental design. 
- 0–2 years of work experience; internships, research assistantships and thesis work are considered. 
- Demonstrated interest in automating repetitive processes. 
- Strong written communication skills, including the ability to explain technical methods to non-technical colleagues. 
- Interest in advertising, media and business performance; prior media experience is not required. 
 Nice to Have 
- Experience with data modeling, dbt or workflow schedulers. 
- Power BI experience. 
- Experience with site analytics (Google Analytics, Adobe Analytics) or ad platform APIs. 
- Exposure to causal inference, marketing mix modeling or incrementality testing. 
- Experience using LLMs or AI tools to automate analysis or query data. 
- A thesis, research project or open-source work available for review. 
 Why Join Involved Media? 
- Hybrid work schedule in NYC. 
- Exposure to cross-channel campaigns with top clients. 
- Collaborative, supportive team with room to grow into senior leadership. 
- Competitive compensation, benefits, and opportunities for advancement. 
 About AMS 
 AMS is a global media solutions company built on growth for the brands we serve and the people who power us. 
 Across our brands Active International, XACTV, and Involved Media, we connect talent, technology, and insight to help leading companies grow. 
 Recognized globally as a Great Place to Work, we invest in our people with the same care, curiosity, and long-term commitment we bring to our clients.

- We grow together. Your growth drives our success.

AMS offers a very competitive benefits package inclusive of medical coverage, dental, vision, disability, 401k, paid time off, community engagement opportunities, great colleagues, and great learning opportunities.

title: Senior Analyst | Involved Media | NYC
description:
About the role 
 Most analytics roles report on what happened. This role helps clients decide what to do next, connecting media performance to the business results their leadership is measured on. 
 The Senior Analyst develops a deep understanding of a portfolio of clients' businesses and uses that knowledge to guide what is measured and recommended. Clients span direct-to-consumer retail, healthcare, nonprofit fundraising and higher education, and each measures success differently: orders, enrollments, donations, applications. The role requires interpreting those results in the context of each client's overall business, not only its media plan. 
 Examples of questions the Senior Analyst helps clients answer: 
- How many additional orders will another $500K in media drive during the holiday season? 
- Which markets should we expand into next year, and what will it cost to acquire a member there? 
- Is our marketing growing applications, or capturing students who would have applied anyway? 
- After a softer-than-expected quarter, how should we reforecast donations for the rest of the year? 
 What you'll do 
 Analytics 
- Lead the analytical story for monthly and quarterly business reviews. 
- Analyze complex data sets to identify performance anomalies, market shifts and platform baseline trends, and translate findings into clear storylines for business reviews and executive presentations. 
- Use client, site and platform data to answer client business questions and develop practical recommendations. 
- Coordinate with cross-functional teams to streamline project timelines, document technical workflows and standardize best practices. 
- Use scripting to automate analysis, data cleansing and data integration tasks.

- Partner with data science and client service teams to build and maintain budget forecasting models that support media efficiency and account growth.

- 3–5 years of experience in marketing analytics, performance marketing, advertising or a related field preferred. 
- Bachelor's degree in a quantitative or analytical field (economics, statistics, mathematics, engineering, finance or similar). 
- Strong statistical skills, including regression, forecasting, test design and significance testing. 
- Hands-on proficiency in SQL and Python or R, with the ability to pull and test data independently. 
- Working knowledge of MMM, multi-touch attribution and incrementality testing, including what each can and cannot measure, and the ability to evaluate vendor results.

- Ability to present data-driven recommendations with confidence and to propose workable alternatives when a request is not feasible.

- Experience in direct-to-consumer, healthcare, nonprofit or higher education marketing.

- Experience with site analytics (Google Analytics, Adobe Analytics). 
- Master's degree or MBA with a quantitative focus.

CleanSpark (Nasdaq: CLSK), is a market-leading data center developer with a proven track record of success. We control a portfolio of more than 1.8 GW of power, land, and data centers across the United States powered by globally competitive energy prices. Sitting at the intersection of Bitcoin, energy, operational excellence, and capital stewardship, we optimize our infrastructure to deliver superior returns to our shareholders. Monetizing low-cost, high reliability energy by producing a global emerging critical resource – compute – positions us to prosper in an ever-changing world. 

Visit our website at www.cleanspark.com.


Job Overview
The Commercial Operations Associate supports CleanSpark’s AI data center projects through procurement, contract administration, and financial analysis. Reporting to the Senior Manager, Commercial Operations, this role evaluates vendor proposals, analyzes budget variances, resolves commercial issues, and recommends actions to support project delivery.


Key Responsibilities
- Analyze project budgets, forecasts, and expenditures; recommend actions to address variances.
- Evaluate vendor proposals and recommend suppliers based on cost, terms, delivery, and risk.
- Negotiate commercial terms within delegated authority and coordinate required approvals.
- Review contracts and change orders; recommend responses to commercial risks and vendor issues.
- Investigate and resolve nonroutine procurement, invoice, and payment discrepancies.
- Apply commercial policies and financial controls, escalating matters outside delegated authority.
- Improve procurement, contract administration, and financial reporting processes.
- Prepare reports highlighting commercial trends, risks, and recommended actions.
- Maintain accurate commercial records and project data in company systems.
- Coordinate agreements, vendor onboarding, and approvals with Legal and business partners.
- Partner with project teams and vendors to resolve commercial issues and support project delivery.
- Support audits and compliance reviews; recommend corrective actions.
- Perform additional duties as assigned.
 This role requires professionalism, respect, strong communication, and the ability to work well with others in a team-oriented, inclusive environment.

Required Qualifications
- Bachelor’s degree in business, finance, construction management, operations, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
- Two or more years of relevant experience in commercial operations, procurement, financial analysis, or contract administration.
- Experience independently evaluating commercial issues and making business recommendations.
- Ability to analyze budgets, evaluate vendor proposals, and review commercial terms.
- Sound judgment in applying policies, resolving nonroutine issues, and recognizing approval requirements.
- Proficiency with Microsoft Office and experience with project or financial systems such as Oracle Primavera Cloud, Unifier, Tipalti, or NetSuite.
- Strong analytical, organizational, and communication skills.
- Ability to travel and support time-sensitive business needs as required.

Preferred Qualifications
- Experience in data centers, construction, engineering, energy, or other capital-intensive industries.
- Experience with vendor negotiations, commercial risk, change orders, or procurement and financial process improvements.

This position may involve duties that require operation of a company vehicle or travel between job sites.  As such, candidates must be insurable under CleanSpark's vehicle insurance policy.

It provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation, and training.

title: Financial Planning & Business Intelligence Analyst
description:
About Us
 We are the team behind Envelopes.com, JAM Paper, and Folders.com. For decades, businesses, schools, organizations, and consumers have trusted us for high-quality envelopes, stationery, folders, labels, and office products.
 Our brands have long histories and strong reputations, but we are building for what comes next. We are investing heavily in ecommerce, AI, customer experience, and experimentation to create a faster, smarter, more customer-centric organization.
 About the Role
 We are seeking an Financial Planning & Business Intelligence Analyst to support financial planning and help teams across the business turn data into actionable insights. This role combines budgeting, forecasting, and financial analysis with sales reporting and broader business analytics.
 Reporting to our Chief Analytics Officer, you will work closely with Finance, Sales, and Operations to explain business performance, identify opportunities, and support better decisions. You will also support our planned implementation of Microsoft Fabric, helping establish reliable data, consistent metrics, and effective reporting.
 The ideal candidate brings a strong financial foundation, hands-on NetSuite experience, and the ability to understand, validate, and analyze data across business systems.
 Financial Planning and Analysis 
- Support annual budgeting, recurring forecasts, and long-term financial planning in partnership with Finance and business leaders, and build and maintain financial models that evaluate revenue, expenses, profitability, and business initiatives.
- Analyze actual results against budget, forecast, and prior periods, explain key drivers and variances, and prepare monthly management reporting with clear insights into performance, risks, and opportunities.
 Sales and Business Analytics 
- Analyze sales performance by customer, product, channel, and other business segments, identifying trends in revenue, volume, pricing, product mix, and gross margin.
- Develop dashboards and recurring reports that help teams track KPIs, and support ad hoc analysis on customer profitability, operational efficiency, and growth opportunities.
- Partner with stakeholders across the business to translate questions into analyses and practical recommendations, presenting both the results and their business implications clearly.
 NetSuite and Data Quality 
- Use NetSuite to extract, organize, and analyze financial and transactional data, creating and maintaining saved searches, reports, and dashboards, and understanding how customers, items, transactions, and accounts relate to one another and affect reporting.
- Combine NetSuite data with other business data sources, validate accuracy, reconcile business reporting to financial results, and investigate discrepancies.
- Document metric definitions, data sources, and reporting logic to improve consistency and confidence in reporting.
 Microsoft Fabric and Reporting Improvements 
- Support the planned Microsoft Fabric implementation by gathering business requirements, defining reporting needs, prioritizing analytics use cases, and partnering with technical teams so data from NetSuite and other systems supports financial and operational reporting.
- Help validate migrated data, test datasets and dashboards, reconcile new reporting with existing sources, and contribute to Power BI dashboards and shared reporting datasets as the platform is implemented.
- Identify opportunities to automate recurring reporting and reduce manual spreadsheet work, and help business users understand and adopt new reports, dashboards, and metric definitions.
 AI-Enabled Ways of Working 
- Use approved AI and automation tools to speed up analysis, reporting, and documentation, while verifying outputs and applying sound judgment to the results.
 Requirements 
 Required Qualifications
- Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business Analytics, Information Systems, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
- 2–4 years of experience in FP&A, financial analysis, business analytics, or a similar role.
- Hands-on experience using NetSuite for financial reporting, saved searches, and data analysis.
- Strong Excel skills, including financial modeling, pivot tables, and advanced formulas.
- Solid understanding of financial statements, accounting fundamentals, and business performance metrics.
- Working knowledge of U.S.-based financial systems and accounting practices, including U.S. GAAP.
- Strong data skills, including the ability to clean, combine, validate, and analyze datasets and understand relationships across data sources.
- Ability to translate business questions into structured analysis and explain findings to financial and nonfinancial stakeholders.
- Strong attention to detail, problem-solving skills, and the ability to manage competing priorities.
 Preferred Qualifications
- Familiarity with Microsoft Fabric; experience supporting a data or analytics platform implementation is a plus.
- Experience building reports and dashboards in Power BI.
- Experience using SQL to query, join, and analyze data.
- Familiarity with Power Query or other tools used to automate data preparation and reporting.
- Experience analyzing sales, customer profitability, pricing, and product margins.
- Experience gathering reporting requirements, validating data, and supporting user acceptance testing.
 You’ll Thrive Here If You
- Take pride in delivering accurate, timely forecasts and reporting that leaders can rely on.
- Enjoy explaining the “why” behind financial and sales performance in clear, practical terms.
- Care about consistent metrics and want people across the business to trust their data.
- Are excited to help shape a new analytics platform and make reporting faster, more automated, and more useful.

Our operating companies rely on you to run a predictable forecasting cycle, get newly acquired companies up to speed, and help them improve how they manage working capital.  Continuous improvement mindset - you look for ways to make each cycle faster, cleaner, and more automated, and you document the process so it runs the same way every time.
 Sound judgment - you handle bank access, payments, and confidential financial information with care, and you know when to escalate.

Your core responsibilities will be maintaining the rolling forecast and producing weekly pipeline reporting, translating changes in commercial activity, delivery capacity, and hiring into a clear view of financial performance and priorities. You will help design and build AI-enabled systems and workflows that improve the quality, speed, and repeatability of finance work.  - Have demonstrated hands-on experience using AI tools for substantive financial analysis, with the judgment to verify data, calculations, and conclusions and develop repeatable workflows.

LOCATION

This is a fully remote role open to candidates based anywhere in the US.

Finance · Remote (US) · Full-time · Reports to Director of Finance




ABOUT NEST

Nest builds care plan infrastructure for veterinary hospitals. Corporate veterinary groups use Nest to run preventive care memberships under their own brand, and we handle what sits underneath: enrollment, recurring billing, analytics, marketing, and seller-of-record compliance.

Care plans change how pets receive care. Pet owners pay a predictable monthly amount, visit more often, and catch problems earlier. Hospitals build steadier revenue and longer client relationships. Our mission is to make that kind of preventive care available to every pet.




ABOUT THE TEAM

Finance at Nest is led by our Director of Finance and works closely with both founders and with leaders across Sales, Operations, Product, and Engineering. The team owns planning, board and investor reporting, and the financial models behind enterprise sales.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

Our financial models have two audiences. Internally, they guide how we plan, hire, and raise capital. Externally, they help a large veterinary network decide whether to partner with us, and the EBITDA lift model and pricing proposal are often what a network's CFO evaluates before signing. You will spend about 70% of your time on FP&A and about 30% on customer-facing modeling. The work rewards people who ask why a number is what it is, can turn a vague question into a structured analysis, and care whether the reader understands the answer. After a year, you will own the operating model, the board package, and the standard enterprise proposal model, and the sales team will bring you into late-stage deals as a matter of course.




RESPONSIBILITIES

FP&A (about 70%)

 - Maintain and extend the operating model, including the revenue forecast, expenses, cash flow, and runway.

 - Prepare the monthly management report and the board package.

 - Lead model design and variance analysis for the annual budget and reforecasts, working directly with department leads.

 - Track unit economics by segment and by hospital, including acquisition cost, lifetime value, gross margin, and contribution margin.

 - Build investor-ready models, scenario analyses, and data room materials during fundraising.

 - Build and maintain management reporting and self-service dashboards in Sigma.

Customer-facing modeling (about 30%)

 - Maintain the EBITDA lift model and unit economics framework we present to enterprise prospects.

 - Model custom proposals across adoption levels, plan designs, fee structures, and rebates, showing the effect on both the customer's economics and Nest's margins.

 - Model revenue recognition for enterprise customers under ASC 606, including allocation, consumption-based recognition, straight-line amortization, and breakage.

 - Join customer calls when a CFO or procurement team wants to test assumptions on incrementality and ROI.

 - Analyze performance across our live hospitals, including spend lift, visit frequency, cancellations, breakage, and payment capture.
   
   


WHO YOU ARE

We are looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements for this role. If you meet them, we encourage you to apply. Preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.




MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS

 - You have 4 or more years in FP&A, investment banking, consulting, or finance at a SaaS or healthcare company.

 - You build financial models that are clean, auditable, and ready to show a board or a customer.

 - You write your own SQL against a warehouse such as BigQuery or Snowflake.

 - You understand SaaS economics, including ARR, retention, CAC, LTV, and payback, and the accounting underneath them.

 - You have presented analysis to senior audiences and handled hard questions about it.


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Experience with Sigma, Looker, Tableau, or a similar BI tool.

 - Working knowledge of ASC 606 and subscription billing.

 - Experience with Stripe, QuickBooks, or similar billing and accounting systems.

 - Experience at a venture-backed company at seed or Series A.
   
   


HOW WE WORK

Nest is a small, fully remote team. Each person owns outcomes the company depends on, and the scope of most roles grows as the company does. We write decisions down, give direct feedback, and expect problems to be raised early. The work is demanding because hospitals and pet owners rely on it every day, and it suits people who want more ownership than a larger company would offer.





OUR HIRING PROCESS

Our process typically includes a conversation with the hiring manager, a working session based on the actual job, and conversations with the people you would work with most. We will tell you what each stage covers before it starts, and we close the loop with everyone we interview.




EQUAL OPPORTUNITY

Nest is an equal opportunity employer. We make hiring decisions based on the work and the person, without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic. If you need accommodation during the hiring process, email recruiting@nestveterinary.com.

- Turnaround & Restructuring (T&R)
- Strategic Performance Solutions (SPS)
- Retail Performance Improvement (RPI)
- Transaction Advisory (TA)
- Transaction & Valuation Opinions (VAL)
 We partner with companies, private equity firms, and private credit lenders to drive measurable financial and operational improvement. Our Finance Excellence vertical focuses on transforming the Office of the CFO – building the processes, talent, reporting infrastructure, and operating discipline that high-performing businesses need.
 We are hands-on operators. Our teams work directly with management, move quickly, and deliver results that are visible on the income statement and balance sheet. We advise organizations on finance transformation, operational improvement, performance management, and transaction-related initiatives. - Strong knowledge of FAR/DFARS and earned value management (EVM) principles a plus.

 As a Financial Analyst on the Account Management team, you will serve as the primary data subject matter expert (SME) and the strategic bridge between our client-facing teams and the Data Analysis/Reporting department. Your mission is to translate complex pharmacy benefit data into actionable financial insights for our clients. You will be a trusted advisor to both internal Account Management leadership and client financial teams, ensuring that every strategic decision is backed by rigorous analysis and a deep understanding of SmithRx financial components.

- Support the resolution of complex client scenarios by conducting deep-dive data research and root-cause analysis.

- 5+ years of experience in data analysis, financial underwriting, or actuarial support within the healthcare and/or PBM industry.
- Strong command of data visualization tools (e.g., Looker, Tableau, PowerBI) and advanced Excel skills (VLOOKUPs, Pivot Tables, modeling).

description:
Job Title: Budgeting/Forecasting Specialist
 Position Type: Full-Time, Remote
 Working Hours: U.S. client business hours
 About the Role: 
 Our client is seeking a Budgeting/Forecasting Specialist to build financial models, manage planning cycles, and provide forward-looking insights that guide strategy. This role requires strong analytical skills, mastery of modeling tools, and the ability to translate numbers into actionable recommendations. You will work closely with finance leaders and department heads to ensure budgets and forecasts are accurate, realistic, and strategically aligned.
 Responsibilities :
 Budget Development:
- Lead preparation of annual operating and capital budgets.
- Consolidate inputs across departments and business units.
- Ensure budgets align with company goals and resource constraints.
 Forecasting:
- Maintain rolling forecasts for revenue, expenses, and cash flow.
- Update models monthly or quarterly with actuals, adjusting assumptions.
- Build scenario and sensitivity analyses to test potential outcomes.
 Variance Analysis:
- Compare actual results to budgets/forecasts.
- Prepare written commentary to explain variances and recommend corrective actions.
 Financial Modeling:
- Build dynamic Excel or Google Sheets models (DCF, ROI, IRR, break-even).
- Use advanced formulas, macros, or BI tool integrations to improve accuracy.
 Reporting:
- Prepare management reporting packages with dashboards and visualizations.
- Present insights to executives, highlighting risks and opportunities.
 Collaboration:
- Partner with department heads to align forecasts with operational plans.
- Work with FP&A teams to refine planning assumptions.
 Process Improvement:
- Identify inefficiencies in forecasting workflows.
- Implement new FP&A software or improve data integrations (Adaptive Insights, Anaplan, Workday, or equivalent).
 What Makes You a Perfect Fit: 
- Highly analytical with an eye for detail.
- Comfortable building models from scratch and explaining them simply.
- Proactive in identifying trends, risks, and opportunities.
- Skilled communicator who can influence leaders through data-driven storytelling.
 Required Experience & Skills (Minimum): 
- Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or related field.
- 3+ years in financial planning/analysis, budgeting, or forecasting.
- Advanced Excel/Google Sheets (nested formulas, pivot tables, sensitivity modeling).
- Experience preparing variance analyses for leadership.
 Ideal Experience & Skills: 
- FP&A tool experience (Anaplan, Adaptive Insights, Hyperion, Workday).
- MBA, CFA, or CPA credential.
- Experience forecasting for SaaS, real estate, or professional services.
- Familiarity with BI/analytics platforms (Power BI, Tableau, Looker).
 What Does a Typical Day Look Like? 
 A Budgeting/Forecasting Specialist’s day revolves around building clarity about the future of the business. You will:
- Maintain financial models — updating them with actuals and revising assumptions based on market or internal trends.
- Analyze variances — reviewing how actual results differ from plan and preparing written explanations with supporting data.
- Support decision-making — running scenario analyses (“what happens if revenue grows 15%?” “what if headcount increases by 20?”) and presenting implications to leadership.
- Collaborate across teams — meeting with department managers to validate budget assumptions and ensure spending aligns with strategy.
- Deliver reporting — packaging forecasts and analyses into dashboards and executive-ready presentations.
- Continuously improve — refining models, implementing forecasting software, and streamlining inputs to shorten cycles.
 In essence: the role is about ensuring the organization has reliable forward-looking data to guide strategy, supported by strong financial models and clear commentary.
 Key Metrics for Success (KPIs): 
- Forecast accuracy within ±5–10%.
- Budget completion within agreed timelines.
- Variance explanations delivered within 2–3 days of close.
- Models updated regularly and free from errors.
- Forecasting cycle time is reduced via automation.

- Initial Phone Screen
- Video Interview with Pavago Recruiter
- Practical Task (e.g., build a simple forecast model and run sensitivity analysis)
- Client Interview
- Offer & Background Verification

Flosum is a growth-stage company operating with the intensity and speed of a startup backed by the discipline of a mature operator.
 The Role 
 We're hiring a SaaS Revenue & Financial Analyst who will own the measurement layer of our entire business. You will be the person who knows every number — ARR, net retention, expansion, churn, pipeline conversion, cost of acquisition, gross margin by product line, services margin, cash flow, and everything in between. You'll work across Salesforce (our CRM and billing system of record) and QuickBooks (our financial system) to build a unified, always-current picture of company performance.
 This is not a reporting role. This is an analytical role where you connect revenue operations data to financial outcomes and surface the insights that drive decisions at the CEO level.
 What You'll Own 
 You will build and maintain our SaaS metrics infrastructure — ARR waterfall, cohort retention analysis, revenue recognition schedules, deferred revenue tracking, and unit economics by segment. You will reconcile Salesforce bookings data against QuickBooks revenue entries and ensure we have a single source of truth across both systems. You will produce monthly and quarterly financial and revenue packages for leadership, including variance analysis against plan. You will model scenarios for pricing changes, product bundling, geographic expansion, and headcount investment. You will monitor pipeline health and translate pipeline data into revenue forecasts with documented assumptions. You will own the data integrity between our CRM and accounting systems, flagging discrepancies before they compound. You will support board-level and investor-level reporting with clean, defensible metrics.
 Requirements 
 What We're Looking For 
 You have three-plus years of experience in SaaS financial analysis, revenue operations, or FP&A at a B2B software company. You are deeply proficient in Salesforce — not as a user, but as someone who understands opportunity objects, product schedules, contract structures, and reporting at a data level. You are equally proficient in QuickBooks Online, including chart of accounts design, revenue categorization, journal entries, and reconciliation workflows. You understand ASC 606 revenue recognition principles and can apply them to a multi-product SaaS business with annual and multi-year contracts. You can build financial models from scratch in Excel or Google Sheets — not from templates, from logic. You think in terms of cohorts, not just totals. You understand the difference between bookings, billings, and revenue, and you can explain why each matters. You are precise, skeptical of your own numbers, and obsessive about data integrity.
 Preferred 
 Experience at a company with a mix of subscription revenue and professional services. Familiarity with Salesforce CPQ or native Salesforce quoting and contract objects. Exposure to investor or board reporting at a growth-stage company. Experience with Marketo or HubSpot data as it relates to CAC and attribution modeling.
 Why Flosum 
 You'll report directly into the CEO's operating rhythm. Your work will not sit in a queue — it will shape hiring plans, product investment, and go-to-market strategy in real time. Flosum is building the definitive platform for Salesforce lifecycle management, and we need someone who can measure every dimension of that growth with precision.

title: Portfolio CEO Network
description:
ABOUT AMERICAN OPERATOR

American Operator exists to keep the American Dream alive through small-business leadership & ownership. We place experienced operators into businesses of retiring owners who want their life’s work placed in capable, values-driven hands. Our mission is to ensure great businesses stay local, stay strong, and stay in the hands of leaders who care.

Operators who partner with us step into the CEO role of an established company and receive the support, coaching, and community needed to grow it for the next generation. Over time, they follow a clear pathway toward becoming a significant equity owner if growth targets are met.




IS THIS YOU?

 - Are you a proven industry pro who’s ready to build a business for yourself?

 - Do you want to lead a business end-to-end instead of managing one slice of it?

 - Have you dreamed of running your own business but haven’t had the idea or chance?

 - Do you care deeply about people, service, and building organizations that last?

 - Would you relocate for the right long-term opportunity to build your future?




THE OPPORTUNITY

By joining our Portfolio CEO Program, you position yourself for future CEO opportunities in an established small business where strong operational leadership is needed most. When an opportunity aligns with your capabilities, we’ll reach out and you’ll work directly with our team to understand the business, align on priorities, and prepare for a successful leadership transition.

As the Portfolio CEO, you’ll run the business with full accountability, driving performance, developing the team, and ensuring stability during and after the handoff. Throughout the journey, American Operator provides leadership transition support, strategic guidance, and a network of peers so you can focus on delivering results and building a long-term path toward ownership.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Lead day-to-day operations and own 100% of the company’s P&L.

 - Manage and develop the existing team to achieve strong execution and accountability.

 - Oversee customer relationships, quality control, and job profitability.

 - Maintain vendor and supplier relationships.

 - Analyze operational data to make informed decisions about pricing, staffing, and capital allocation.

 - Create and execute annual budgets, forecasts, and growth plans.

 - Partner with American Operator and key stakeholders to drive the company’s next stage of success.

 - Build credibility with the existing team, customers, and owner during the transition period.

 - Maintain operational discipline and uphold the company’s legacy and reputation.

 - Deliver measurable improvement in revenue, profitability, and cash flow.

 - Ensure safe, compliant, and efficient operations.

 - Take full ownership of business performance and culture.

 - Demonstrate leadership grounded in accountability, humility, and sound judgment.




MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

 - 10+ years of operational leadership experience in an American Operator target industry. (Preferably Manufacturing, Value-Add Distribution, Flooring, Electrical or Plumbing Services).

 - 5+ years of hiring/firing authority.

 - 5+ years of responsibility over P&L and/or company budgets.

 - Proven success managing teams and complex operations.

 - Small business leadership experience.

 - Excellent communication and relationship management skills.

 - Entrepreneurial mindset with a long-term approach to business building.

 - Must be willing to regionally locate (5-state area)






Compensation: Base salary range of $150,000-$180,000, along with a comprehensive benefits package that may include health coverage, paid time off, and holidays. The role is eligible for additional compensation, including equity participation; the amount varies based on the portfolio company and deal structure.



*Location Disclaimer: Opportunities to lead an American Operator acquisition business are based in various locations across the US and relocation will be required for this role if you are not in a commutable distance from the business. The exact location of the business will be revealed during the interview process.

_______________________________________________________________________________________________________


We are hiring a high-potential early-career teammate to help drive commercial execution across remote monitoring programs, health system partnerships, and state-sponsored initiatives.
 
This role is for someone smart, hungry, organized, and genuinely AI-first. You do not need decades of experience, but you do need strong judgment, high ownership, and the ability to turn messy inputs into clear, useful output fast.
 
You will work across proposals, commercial analysis, internal coordination, follow-up, and day-to-day execution. Some days that may mean building a pricing model or cleaning up a proposal. Commercial execution and proposal support

Turn calls, notes, and rough direction into clear outputs such as recap notes, follow-up emails, action trackers, and decision logs
Keep documents organized, current, and easy to navigate, with strong version control and clean source materials
Help prepare leadership for meetings, follow-ups, and fast-moving commercial discussions
 
Sizing, pricing, and business analysis
Build and maintain Excel or Google Sheets models that help size, price, and compare opportunities
Check assumptions, formulas, and outputs carefully to ensure they are sound and internally consistent
Pull together concise summaries that help leaders understand the opportunity, key decisions, and operational implications
Support lightweight analysis across pipeline, commercial models, and strategic priorities
 
Coordination and follow-through
Keep multiple workstreams moving across timelines, owners, dependencies, and next steps
Maintain a simple, reliable view of active opportunities, including status, next action, and priority
Produce clear weekly updates and meeting prep materials that help leaders make decisions quickly
Follow through without needing repeated reminders
 
AI-first ways of working
Use AI tools such as Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, and similar platforms to accelerate drafting, synthesis, research support, and structured analysis
Build reusable prompts, templates, and workflows that improve speed, consistency, and quality
Look for opportunities to automate repetitive work and simplify how the team operates
Verify outputs carefully, especially anything numerical, customer-facing, or high-stakes

- 1 to 3 years of experience, or clear evidence that you are unusually high output and quick to learn

- Comfort with spreadsheets and basic modeling logic
- High attention to detail and strong ownership mentality
- Natural curiosity about AI tools and enthusiasm for using them to work smarter and faster
- Ability to stay organized and reliable in a fast-moving environment
- Humility, coachability, and genuine appetite for growth
- Good judgment, positive attitude, and willingness to do the work behind the scenes that keeps things moving

Company Culture and Benefits

We’re a dynamic remote-first environment, with offices in Golden, CO and Redwood City, CA and a talented, motivated team of colleagues globally. title: Business Analyst
location: Atlanta, GA; Remote; Hybrid; Charlotte, NC
description:
Business Analyst
Employment Type: Full-Time, Experienced
Department: Information Technology 

CGS is looking for business analysts to work with a large federal agency! As a Business Analyst in Business operations and Content Strategy for CGS, you will partner with internal business owners and external partners to understand new business opportunities and define functional requirements.  

CGS brings motivated, highly skilled, and creative people together to solve the government’s most dynamic problems with cutting-edge technology. To carry out our mission, we are seeking candidates who are excited to contribute to government innovation, appreciate collaboration, and can anticipate the needs of others. Here at CGS, we offer an environment in which our employees feel supported, and we encourage professional growth through various learning opportunities.
 
Skills and attributes for success:
- Support the development of briefings, agendas, and other general documentation support as directed, including training material and demonstration sessions for new and existing technologies to various stakeholders.
- Document and analyze business and functional requirements so that they may be accurately translated into process maps and technical system requirements
- Develop comprehensive documentation that meets organizational standards, to include but not limited to basic system architectural diagrams/wireframes, concepts of operations, monthly status reports
- Create high-level briefings and communications materials for customers, management, and executive stakeholders
- Work with the government and team members to identify, recommend, and implement opportunities for service delivery improvement and new technology implementation
- Evaluate program materials and develop innovative approaches for improvement
- Independently gather information from subject matter experts to develop, organize, and write procedure manuals, technical specifications, and process documentation
- Develop and implement a deep understanding of Microsoft and Atlassian products and services (Teams, SharePoint, Visio, Jira, Confluence) to translate complex product information into simple, polished, and engaging content
- Research, outline, write, and edit new and existing content, working closely with various team members to understand project requirements
- Develop content in various media forms for maximum usability, with a consistent and cohesive voice across all documentation
- Perform risk management, including identifying, prioritizing, and mitigating risks, and communicating and escalating risks and issues
- Support a continuous improvement process by providing recommendations on improving products, services, and processes.
- Manage client interaction and expectations regarding team efforts
- Identify and coordinate cross-team dependencies and collaboration
- Continually seek opportunities to increase customer satisfaction, develop and deepen long-lasting client relationships

Qualifications:
- Must be a U.S. Citizen
- Bachelor's Degree (Computer Science, or engineering)
- Must be able to successfully complete a stringent Background Investigation and obtain required Government Security clearance
- 7+ years of experience in business analysis, systems analysis, and/or design of information systems programs and related business processes
- Experience working with phase-based and Agile delivery methods
- Experience with Jira or other Agile tools
- Ability to clearly communicate technical concepts to both technical and non-technical users.
- Must be able to work well both in a team environment and independently.
- Must possess exceptional attention to detail
- Excellent interpersonal and communication skills
- Familiarity with government projects and policy/procedures teams
- Demonstrates ability to interact comfortably with Senior Leadership and/or Government Executives and staff on a day-to-day basis
- Experience in managing client requirements and small teams
- Excellent analytical skills and business presentation skills
Ideally, you will also have:
- Experience supporting DHS HQ or other US Federal Agencies   
- Experience tracking and reporting project or program delivery progress and  budget execution
- Experience developing project briefs and reports for non-technical audiences 
- Knowledge of the federal acquisition lifecycle
- Familiarity with Business Intelligence and Data Analytics
- Project Management, Agile, and/or Cyber Certifications (PMP / ACP / CSM / SAFe / CISM)
 [...] Contact Government Services (CGS) strives to simplify and enhance government bureaucracy through the optimization of human, technical, and financial resources. We combine cutting-edge technology with world-class personnel to deliver customized solutions that fit our client’s specific needs. We are committed to solving the most challenging and dynamic problems.
For the past seven years, we’ve been growing our government contracting portfolio, and along the way, we’ve created valuable partnerships by demonstrating a commitment to honesty, professionalism, and quality work.
Here at CGS we value honesty through hard work and self-awareness, professionalism in all we do, and to deliver the best quality to our consumers mending those relations for years to come.
 [...] - Health, Dental, and Vision
- Life Insurance
 [...] Join our team and become part of government innovation!
Explore additional job opportunities with CGS on our Job Board:
https://cgsfederal.com/join-our-team/
For more information about CGS please visit: https://www.cgsfederal.com or contact:
Email: info@cgsfederal.com

description:

At any given time, 16 million Americans are experiencing a crisis that requires urgent help from our legal system or government. The right assistance could transform their lives. But today, most never get it.

Atticus makes it easy for any sick or injured American to get life-changing aid. Our mission is to tear down barriers between people in crisis and the aid they deserve. In the last six years, we’ve become the leading platform connecting people with disabilities to government benefits.

We also help victims of accidents, misconduct, and violence get compensation from insurance. So far, we’ve helped hundreds of thousands of people access over $10 billion in life-changing aid —and earned over 20,000 five-star reviews. And we’re just getting started.

We’ve raised more than $100 million from top VC firms like Forerunner, Google Ventures, and True Ventures, and we’re on our way to creating a category defining business assisting Americans in need.

Where we are today:

 - Last year we raised a $50M Series C, valuing Atticus at $450M.

 - Our primary vertical (Disability) is profitable and will reach a ~$90M revenue run-rate by the end of this year

 - We’ve kicked off our Injury vertical with a small but scrappy team working on the offering and GTM approach.


THE JOB

Our business is complex and multi-faceted: We play in an enormous space with huge barriers to entry, we have no direct competitors, and as a two-sided marketplace we have to coordinate multiple constituencies via a complex funnel with some parts that are all tech and others that are fully human. Every day we face new operating challenges that require someone to quickly gather data, make a decision, and execute.

So, in addition to software engineers, lawyers, and marketers, our team includes a bunch of ex-consultants (our CEO is a BCG alum and we’ve built a small BizOps org from BCG, Bain and McKinsey).  - Design, test, and ship a site experiment for our new Injury vertical to qualify and convert clients.

 - Find the gaps in our client service operations and lead the project that cuts our costs to serve each client by 25%.

 - You took on management ahead of tenure (e.g., EM at McKinsey, mini-PL at BCG, Manager at Bain).

LOCATION

This job is fully remote and we’re committed to empowering everyone with flexibility. Work remotely, and travel to LA (on the company dime) as needed to be with your colleagues – usually quarterly, plus offsites. We care a lot about building a great culture and we think some interactions need to happen in person, so we put a lot of thought into retreats, offsites, and other ways to gather.

Wealth management is a $545 billion industry that still runs on manual work. 75% of advisors offer no digital communication beyond email, and most still build financial plans by hand in Excel. Advisors at Savvy service up to 50% more households and save 19 hours a week.

The trajectory is steep and it's still early. We're a Series C company with 170+ people, $200M raised, and $100M ARR in sight this year. Inc. ranked us the No. 1 fastest-growing financial services company in America in 2026. Come build the next stage with us!

WHY HARVEY

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched.

Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.




ROLE OVERVIEW

Customer Experience runs on data — but right now, that data lives in too many places, speaks too many languages, and reaches the wrong people too late. This role exists to fix that.

As Harvey's first Support Operations Data Analyst, you'll own the analytics function for the Customer Experience org. You'll build and maintain the dashboards, reports, and feedback loops that tell us whether we're hitting our north stars — cSAT, TTR, QA scores, escalation rates — and surface the signal underneath the numbers so we can act on it. You'll sit within the Support Operations team, reporting to the Support Operations Manager, and work closely with Customer Experience leadership and Harvey's central data team to ensure the org is equipped with the right instrumentation as we scale.

This is a solo role. You won't have a team beneath you. You will need to be fluent enough in support analytics to hold the function independently, confident enough to push back on how metrics are framed, and fast enough to operate at Harvey's pace.

 


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own recurring reporting for Customer Experience — weekly, monthly, and QBR-ready — tailored to ops, leadership, and cross-functional audiences

 - Translate support data into clear narratives: what's happening, why, and what to do about it

 - Track and maintain north star metrics: cSAT, TTR by tier, QA scores, bug escalation rate to EPD, and First Response Time

 - Build and maintain self-serve dashboards that give the ops team and leadership real-time visibility into support performance

 - Partner with Support Systems to ensure Zendesk is instrumented to capture the data we need

 - Work with Harvey's central data team to connect support data to broader product and customer data sources

 - Identify and close data collection gaps — if we can't measure it, help define how we should

 - Design feedback loops that connect support signals to Product, Engineering, and Customer Success

 - Quantify the operational cost of product bugs, feature gaps, and onboarding failures

 - Contribute to QA analytics as the QA program matures

 - Track ticket deflection, AI/chatbot performance, and self-service effectiveness

 - Measure the impact of AI-driven support — containment rate, escalation rate from AI interactions, resolution quality — and surface findings that drive how we tune and invest in those tools

 - Support ad hoc analytical requests from the Support Operations Manager, Customer Experience leadership, and senior stakeholders

 


WHAT YOU HAVE

Required

 - 3–5 years of experience in analytics, with at least 2 years directly in support operations, customer success operations, or a closely adjacent function

 - Fluency in support platform data — you know how Zendesk (or equivalent) is structured, what data it produces, and what it doesn't
 - SQL proficiency — you can write complex queries against large datasets without hand-holding (CTEs, window functions, joins across schemas)
 - Dashboard experience — you've built and maintained operational dashboards in Looker, Tableau, Sigma, Omni, or equivalent
 - Reporting for multiple audiences — you know the difference between what a frontline manager needs and what a CFO needs, and you build accordingly
 - Strong data storytelling — you don't just present numbers, you write the narrative
 - Comfort operating solo — you don't need a team around you to deliver, and you don't need a ticket to tell you what to look at
Strong Plus
 - Experience with Python for data manipulation or automation
 - Familiarity with dbt or similar data transformation tooling
 - Experience building or contributing to QA analytics programs
 - Background supporting enterprise SaaS or AI-native products
 - Experience working with Zendesk APIs or extracting data beyond standard reporting
Key Attributes
 - AI-native: you use AI tooling actively in your analytical workflows — not as a novelty, but as a force multiplier
 - Pace: you move in hours and days, not weeks. You surface findings before anyone has to ask
 - Judgment: you know which metrics matter and which are vanity. You push back when framing is wrong
 - Clarity: your outputs are direct, jargon-free, and actionable. You write for the reader, not yourself
 - Ownership: you treat Customer Experience analytics as your problem to solve, not a ticket queue to process
COMPENSATION
$112,000 - $168,000 USD

AlphaGov delivers public-sector consulting for cities, counties, school systems, special districts, utilities, and related agencies.
