Traversal https://www.traversal.com/?utm_source=chatgpt.com is the AI Site Reliability Engineer (AI SRE) for the enterprise.

Production complexity was already outpacing what engineering teams could manage manually, and AI-generated code is accelerating that gap. Traversal is built for that challenge, autonomously understanding and reasoning across even the largest, most complex production environments to diagnose, fix, and prevent incidents. Our mission is to free engineers from endless firefighting and give them more time to focus on creative, high-impact work.

Today, Traversal operates in mission-critical environments at some of the world’s largest enterprises, including PepsiCo, Nubank, Harvey, and DigitalOcean. Our roots remain deeply embedded in AI research, and we’ve brought together researchers from institutions including MIT, Harvard, Berkeley, Columbia, and Cornell with world-class technical staff and operators from companies like Google, Meta, Datadog, ServiceNow, and Citadel Securities to take on one of the hardest problems for AI to solve. Traversal is backed by Sequoia Capital, Kleiner Perkins, Redpoint Ventures, and Khosla Ventures.


THE ROLE

As a Strategy & Operations hire reporting to the Strategy & Operations Lead, you'll partner on Traversal's highest-priority cross-functional initiatives - from pricing and packaging to getting complex deals across the finish line to making sure we're executing against our annual operating plan. This is a generalist seat, not a narrow lane: you'll be handed ambiguous, high-stakes problems, expected to scope them, build the analysis, and drive them to execution end-to-end.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Own cross-functional strategic projects end-to-end - scoping, analysis, and implementation - partnering with Sales, Product, Finance, and Engineering as needed.

 - Help get complex deals to the finish line - supporting structuring, internal approvals, and cross-functional coordination to clear blockers.

 - Own key parts of the annual operating plan process: track progress against goals, flag risks early, and help leadership course-correct.

 - Build financial and operational models to support decision-making across the business.

 - Build scalable, AI-native systems to streamline workflows and distribute insights across the business.

 - Act as a thought partner to executives on ambiguous, high-stakes problems - bring structure and a point of view, not just analysis.




REQUIREMENTS

 - 4-6 years of experience, ideally 2-3 years in management consulting, investment banking, or private equity, followed by 1-2 years in an operating role at an early-stage startup.

 - Track record of owning ambiguous, cross-functional projects end-to-end with minimal oversight.

 - Strong quantitative and analytical skills; comfortable building structured frameworks from scratch.

 - Excellent written and verbal communication - able to synthesize complex problems into clear recommendations for executives.

 - High ownership mentality - bias toward action, comfortable operating with limited process or precedent.

 - Generalist mindset: excited to work across pricing, deals, planning, and whatever the business needs next, rather than staying in one functional lane.


NICE TO HAVE

 - Financial fluency and experience building models (FP&A, LTV / CAC, pricing models, revenue build, unit economics).

 - Comfort leveraging AI tools to move faster and raise the quality of output (not slop).

 - Prior experience in a deal desk, pricing, or GTM strategy function.


COMPENSATION

We offer competitive compensation, startup equity, health insurance, and additional benefits.

The U.S. base salary range for this full-time, in-person role in New York is $175,000–$250,000, plus equity and benefits. Our salary ranges are based on location, level, and role. Individual compensation is determined by experience, skills, and job-related knowledge.




WHY YOU SHOULD JOIN US

Traversal is a place to take on hard, meaningful problems with real ownership from day one. You'll work alongside people who challenge you to grow, learn constantly, and help define a new category of infrastructure software. We think long term, move quickly, and hold a high bar without taking ourselves too seriously.

We offer competitive salary and equity packages, health insurance, fertility benefits, a great tech setup stipend and flexible time off. Plus lunch & dinner, in-office snacks, team happy hours and outings, an annual company offsite, and plenty of built in time to collaborate across teams.

Traversal is fully in-office, 5 days a week, based in New York near Madison Square Park. We have a collaborative, hard-working culture and are energized by building the future of AI-powered software maintenance.

- Exceptional work ethic and ability to independently create and drive workstreams in a fast-paced, deadline-driven startup environment.

- Dog lovers a plus!

 Who We're Looking For

About Paxos

Today’s financial infrastructure is archaic, expensive, inefficient and risky — supporting a system that leaves out more people than it lets in. So we’re rebuilding it.

We’re on a mission to open the world’s financial system to everyone by enabling the instant movement of any asset, any time, in a trustworthy way. For over a decade, we’ve built blockchain infrastructure that tokenizes, custodies, trades and settles assets for the world's leading financial institutions, like PayPal, Venmo, Mastercard, Interactive Brokers and Charles Schwab.

About the team

You'll be the sole member of our Corporate Development function, working side by side with the executive team on Paxos's fundraising and inorganic growth. You'll partner with executive and product leadership to develop investment theses, and work with teams across the company to make sure deals deliver after they close.

About the role

The Corporate Development Lead serves as the driver of Paxos's inorganic growth strategy, identifying, structuring, and executing acquisitions, and owning process management for our fundraising efforts as we scale. You will own the full M&A lifecycle. You will also support the CEO and CFO on end-to-end fundraise processes, helping tell the Paxos story to the right capital partners at the right time.

What you’ll do

 - Own the M&A process end-to-end:
   
   - Develop Investment and M&A theses by researching and monitoring emerging trends and disruptive companies and deeply understanding Paxos product strategy and overall priorities
   
   - Source, evaluate, and execute acquisitions - lead cross-functional diligence, drive structuring, negotiation, and close
   
   - Build and maintain a live pipeline of targets aligned to Paxos’s strategic priorities across infrastructure, distribution, and regulated capabilities

 - Own fundraising process & investor relations:
   
   - Lead end-to-end equity fundraise processes - drive workstreams, prepare investor materials, build and manage data rooms, coordinate diligence, and control the process timeline; serve as the day-to-day owner ensuring nothing falls through the cracks and the CFO and CEO are focused where they matter most
   
   - Maintain ongoing relationships with current and prospective investors between raises providing regular investor updates

 - Be a strategic partner to the executive team:
   
   - Bring an informed external view - on competitors, market structure, and emerging opportunities - into our strategic planning process; translate what you’re seeing in the market into clear, actionable recommendations for leadership

 - Continue to scale Paxos Ventures. To date, Paxos has made over 25 venture investments across the digital asset space
   
   - Source, evaluate and recommend early stage venture investments that further Paxos strategic priorities
   
   - Partner cross-functionally across the company to support founders and portfolio companies
   
   - Help build our founder community by planning programs and events that convene portfolio companies, investors, and others in the ecosystem

 - Build the corp dev muscle at Paxos: Establish repeatable processes for deal sourcing, evaluation, and integration planning; develop the templates, frameworks, and institutional knowledge that make us faster and sharper with every transaction

About you

We’re looking for someone who is entrepreneurial, analytical and very comfortable operating in ambiguity. You help bring focus and structure to ambiguous situations to chart a clear path forward. You might come from investing (Banking, PE, VC) or a Corp Dev team at a fast-growing (fin)tech company.

 - Proven ability to own a fundraising process end-to-end - managing workstreams, materials, and investor relationships with minimal oversight

description:
About the Role 
 The Strategic Operations team sits between Claims Operations, Account Management, Product, and Finance, and owns the work that moves the business against its margin and service targets. 
 As a Strategic Operations Lead at Reserv, you will play a critical role in driving operational efficiency and supporting key strategic initiatives across the organization. You will be responsible for leading cross-functional projects, analyzing complex business challenges, identifying opportunities for improvement, and implementing strategic and scalable solutions to optimize performance. You will also be involved in gathering and interpreting data, coordinating project execution, and ensuring alignment with company goals. 
 The work spans the organization, from gross margin improvement plans for a line of business to the operating standards and systems the business runs on. This role is ideal for someone who thrives in a fast-paced environment, enjoys solving complex problems, and is eager to contribute to the growth and success of an innovative company. You will be an excellent fit if you came out of strategy consulting, can build the case yourself, and want to own the implementation as well as the recommendation. 
 Duties & Responsibilities 
 Strategic Operator: Own strategic initiatives end to end, from framing the problem through to the change being live in the business. Define scope, objectives, deliverables, and timelines in collaboration with senior leadership, and assemble project teams across product, engineering, claims, and account management. 
 Data-Driven: Build the quantitative and qualitative case to size both the problem and the opportunity, working across claims, finance, account, and operational data as well as the people closest to the work. Translate what you find into a recommendation leadership can decide on, and defend it when it is challenged. 
 Leading with Influence: Drive initiatives through senior stakeholders, building the trust that lets you convene them and hold them to a date. Communicate status and trade-offs proactively, make data-driven decisions on resource allocation, and course-correct before a plan slips rather than after. 
 Results-Oriented: Deliver tangible change rather than recommendations, and manage the work to performance metrics that show whether it is working. Verify the change landed in practice, collect feedback, and carry what you learn into how the next initiative is designed. 
- At least 2 years in management consulting, operational transformation, operations management, or strategic planning roles 
- Experience running cross-functional work against dates, and communicating it to senior leadership 
- Detail-oriented and organized, comfortable carrying several workstreams at once 
- Active use of AI tools in your own work, and interest in applying them to operations and analysis 
- Claims or insurance experience is helpful here and is not required 
- Strong quantitative skills, with comfort building the analysis yourself and working fluently in business intelligence tools (Looker, Tableau, Power BI) 
- Bachelor's degree in Business, Finance, Economics, or a related field; MBA or advanced degree preferred 
 Benefits 
- Generous health-insurance package with nationwide coverage, vision, & dental 
- 401(k) retirement plan with employer matching 
- Competitive PTO policy – we want our employees fresh, healthy, happy, and energized! 
- Generous family leave policy after 8 months of continuous work 
- 100% remote (home-based) role designed to support your work-life balance 
- Apple laptop, large second monitor, and other quality-of-life equipment you may want. Technology is something that should make your life easier, not harder! 
 At Reserv, we value diversity in backgrounds, perspectives, and life experiences and believe that diversity in viewpoints and critical thinking drives innovation, first-principles thinking, and success. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and encourage those from all walks of life to apply. If you believe you are a good fit for this role, we would love to hear from you! 
 About Reserv 
 Reserv is an insurtech creating and incubating cutting-edge AI and automation technology to bring efficiency and simplicity to claims. Founded by insurtech veterans with deep experience in SaaS and digital claims, Reserv is venture-backed by Bain Capital and Altai Ventures and began operations in May 2022. We are focused on automating highly manual tasks to tackle long-standing problems in claims and set a new standard for TPAs, insurance technology providers, and adjusters alike. We have ambitious (but attainable!) goals and need people who can work in an evolving environment. If building a leading TPA and the prospect of tackling the long-standing challenges of the claims role sounds exciting, we can't wait to meet you. 
 Location Requirement 
 Candidates must reside in an eligible U.S. state throughout employment. We are unable to hire candidates residing in California, Alaska, Hawaii, U.S. territories, or outside the United States.

title: Business Insights Analyst, Remote US
description:
About Carewell
 Are you an impact-driven problem solver who is passionate about making a difference in the lives of others while contributing to a fast growing start-up? Join Carewell and be a part of a team that creates impactful solutions for caregivers and their unique challenges. We're looking for hardworking individuals committed to raising the bar and striving for impact, scalability, and simplicity. Build your career with Carewell, a category-defining business dedicated to making caregiving easier.
 Our Data Philosophy
 We build for leverage, not volume. That means self-service by default — stakeholders should be able to answer their own questions, with us as partners on the analysis that actually requires one. It means building everything so it can be used by LLMs, not just people; AI tooling isn't perfect, but we'd rather work at its edge than wait for it to be easy. And it means impact above all: we prioritize work with a measurable effect on the business, and we say no to work that doesn't move it forward.
 About the Role
 Carewell runs on a mix of e-commerce fundamentals and service delivery — merchandising, marketing, and revenue on one side; Care Services and customer support on the other. As the Business Insights Analyst, your role exists to make sure every part of that business can see, in numbers, whether it's working.
 You won't be reporting the news. You'll be figuring out what's actually driving the number to move, building the report or tracker that lets a stakeholder self-monitor going forward, and helping them land on the levers worth pulling next. You'll work across financial reporting, marketing efficiency, merchandising and margin, customer cohort behavior, and Care Services productivity — not as a subject matter expert in any one of them, but as someone who's demonstrated, repeatedly, that they can get fluent in a new part of a business fast enough to build something useful in it.
 This role reports to the Sr. Director of Analytics & Data Engineering, who owns the canonical data model and BI architecture. You won't own that architecture — but you'll work inside it daily, and you'll need to understand table structure well enough to direct how existing tables should be re-engineered to support the analysis you're building.
 This is a role built for someone who wants to go deep on the analysis and the business itself, not climb toward people management. We're looking for 3–5 years of experience and someone who's genuinely excited about spending the next several years getting better at this craft, not treating it as a one-year stepping stone.
 What You’ll Do
 Build Reports That Drive Action, Not Just Reporting 
- Design and build reports and dashboards that help stakeholders self-monitor their part of the business
- Go beyond "what happened" to "what's driving it" — identify the underlying business drivers behind metric movement
- Partner with stakeholders to use data to drive strategic business decisions
- Help identify the KPIs a given team or function should actually be watching, and build the reporting that tracks them on an ongoing basis
- Build and maintain monthly financial reports, incorporating light financial analysis across revenue, margin, and cost lines
- Retire or simplify reports that no longer drive decisions, so stakeholders aren't left sorting signal from noise
 Work Across the Business 
- Marketing efficiency analysis: CAC, LTV, spend efficiency, channel-level performance
- Merchandising, revenue, and profit/margin analysis: product- and category-level performance, margin drivers
- Customer cohort behavior: retention curves, repeat purchase patterns, Autoship performance
- Care Services productivity analysis: throughput, service-level metrics, staffing efficiency
- No single one of these needs to be a specialty coming in — you'll need to show you can ramp into a new analytical domain and produce something useful, not just competent, in it
 Turn Feedback Into Measurable Levers 
- Take stakeholder input — a hunch, a complaint, an open question — and turn it into a concrete, testable hypothesis about what lever to pull

- 3–5 years of experience in analytics, business intelligence, reporting, or a closely related analytical role
- Demonstrated experience working across multiple functional areas of a business (i.e. marketing, product, finance, operations)
- Strong SQL skills — comfortable writing complex analytical queries independently, including joins across multiple tables and aggregations at different levels of grain
- Working understanding of relational table structure and data modeling concepts — able to read an existing schema and identify where it should change to support new analysis
- Proven experience with modern reporting tools (Hex, Looker, Omni, Etc.)
- Practical, hands-on experience using AI tools (e.g., Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, or similar) to accelerate analytical work — able to apply this productively from day one, not as something to be trained on
- E-commerce or DTC experience strongly preferred; service-business experience (support, care, or operations) also valuable given Carewell's Care Services function
- A specific example, from a past role, of a report or metric you built that changed a stakeholder's decision — not just informed it

description:
ABOUT ARCA

Arca is a wealth management firm built from the ground up with AI. Most people get financial advice that's reactive: an annual check-in, a plan that's a document instead of a living thing, a relationship where you're one of three hundred clients your advisor is trying to remember. We think that's backwards. The kind of service that used to require a team of specialists behind you, the kind that makes you feel like the only person in the room, should be available to far more than the ultra-wealthy.



So we're building it. We're not SaaS — we are the wealth management business, rebuilding it from the inside with AI. Our platform is an Iron Man suit for advisors: it takes over the low-leverage work so they can focus on what actually requires a human, showing up with empathy, context, and judgment. Underneath, it keeps a living understanding of each client. It remembers the thing you mentioned once, six months ago. It notices when your life changes — a new job, a new kid, a market shift — and adjusts before you think to ask. You won't see the technology. You'll just notice your advisor seems to know you better than any financial professional ever has.



That's the product we're growing: client by client, on the strength of the experience itself. We started by acquiring firms managing over $1B in client assets, which gave us real advisors, real clients, and real financial outcomes to build against from day one. But acquisition was the starting line. The bet is that an advisor backed by this platform delivers something good enough that clients come to us on their own.



It's a $20T market, and we think it's ready to be rebuilt.

Abacum is the leading Business Planning solution for finance teams to drive performance. By automating reporting, enabling collaboration, and simplifying planning and forecasting, we help finance teams shift from number crunching to driving strategic decisions.



Founded in 2020 by two former CFOs, we’ve grown into a global team of 100+ people across 30+ nationalities. Headquartered in New York, we have offices in Toronto and Barcelona. We’re trusted by industry leaders such as Dish Networks, Strava, BetterUp, Kajabi, JG Wentworth, Abridge, Cortex, and hundreds more.



We have raised over $100m, closing in June 2025 our $60M Series B, led by Scale Venture Partners, with the strong participation of Cathay Innovation, Y Combinator, Atomico, Creandum, and angel operators from Adyen, Zapier, and Twitch.



Our mission is ambitious and we can’t do it alone - join Abacum as we build the future of Business Planning!


This is a hard role to put in a box, which is intentional. The Strategic Initiatives Lead will report to the Chief of Staff and work on the problems that matter most to the business right now — not a fixed function. The first projects will likely sit in Growth and then move to GTM broadly speaking, but where you go next depends on what the company needs and what you're good at/eager to learn.

People who've done this well tend to come from places where the feedback loop was short and the expectations were high — early-stage startups, ex-consultants, strategy roles that bled into execution, or careers where they had to build without a playbook.

We're hiring for a specific way of thinking more than a specific background. This role requires someone with high agency and an extreme sense of ownership. If you build, test, and think from first principles, we want to talk.



WHAT YOU'LL OWN

 - Find the wedge: We already have a solid foundation and strong demand generation motion but now it’s time to scale. Your job will be to figure out which channels, which content formats, which distribution motions actually produce predictable pipeline. You run that as a structured research problem, not a campaign calendar.

 - Operate AI-natively: Automate what used to take a team. Build the infrastructure you need to build a real demand engine. Clay for enrichment, n8n for workflows, AI in the loop wherever it replaces manual work. The expectation isn't just that you know these tools, it's that you build with them and enable others to do the same.

 - Own the outcome: You will be tasked with tackling a focused problem or work stream at any given time — scoped with the Chief of Staff, owned by you end to end. The research, structuring, and execution that turns an ambiguous question into a clear recommendation or a running program.

 - Write the playbook: Your wins don't stay with you. What works becomes repeatable and the motion the rest of the team runs as well as the foundation the function is built on. When we find winning plays, scale them, hand them off to the team and start working on the next experiment.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - You're fast because you're structured, not because you're cutting corners. You can sit with ambiguity long enough to form a real point of view, then act on it decisively and with speed.

 - Strong technical and analytical skills and fluency with data, with the ability to work with metrics and data to inform strategy, pressure-test assumptions, and translate findings into clear, actionable plans

 - You're AI-pilled. You have an opinion on where each function should be leveraging AI and are eager to bring others along with you.

 - A bias to action and comfort with ambiguity. You don't wait for a brief; you proactively look for opportunities and build towards them.



WHY TAKE IT

AI is changing how buyers find software faster than most demand teams are adapting. The FP&A category is growing and Abacum is at the forefront.

Most roles put you in a lane. This one doesn't. You'll have visibility into how a Series B company makes decisions, direct access to the Chief of Staff and senior leadership, and a portfolio of projects that actually ships. If you want to figure out what kind of operator you are, this is the place to do it.

Benefits

 - Competitive compensation including equity package

 - Competitive vacation policy

 - Medical Insurance

 - L&D budget

 - Access to Meditopia (wellbeing platform)

 - Language courses (English / Spanish)



Our Values


Customer Obsession: Our purpose is to create value for the finance teams we serve. We pour our energy into driving impact for them fast, and we measure our success by theirs.



Relentless Ambition: We chose to compete at the top alongside the best. We set ambitious goals, and keep pushing when it gets hard. Nothing worth having comes easy.



One Team: There is no “they” at Abacum: “their” problem is our problem. We’re candid because we care, we help each other grow, and we embrace different perspectives.



Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender perception or identity, national origin, age, marital status, protected veteran status, or disability status.

description:
Highbeam is building the future of business banking and cash management.

Our platform combines AI agents, automated financial workflows, and integrated financial products that save brands time and money.

Customers have generated billions in sales and include well-known brands such as Cuts https://www.cutsclothing.com/, Tushy https://hellotushy.com/, Rocco https://roccofridge.com, Sabah https://www.sabah.am/, Still Here https://www.stillhere.nyc/, Alice Mushrooms https://alicemushrooms.com/, Original Grain https://www.originalgrain.com/, birddogs https://www.birddogs.com/, and more.

Our team includes alumni of Shopify, Square, Toast, Rippling, and McKinsey.

We’ve raised $42M in equity from Acrew, FirstMark, Mayfield, and Two Sigma Ventures.



[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/7f0a2d9f-58d8-4b30-b1d9-7e652dfbd66d/962259dc-2fcd-40ed-8403-289c8a933cc7/image.png]

About Highbeam
Highbeam is a banking and lending platform built for e-commerce and consumer packaged goods (CPG) brands. We give founders and finance teams one place to manage cash, pay bills, and access capital — including revolving lines of credit, working capital loans, and card products designed around how product businesses actually operate.

Our lending book is funded in part through institutional debt facilities. As the portfolio grows, so does the need for rigorous facility management and lender reporting.

The Role
We're hiring a Capital Markets Manager to own the day-to-day management and reporting of Highbeam's debt facilities. You'll run the monthly lender reporting cycle, keep us in compliance with facility covenants, manage funding into the facility, and be the first point of contact for our lenders.

This is a hands-on role at the intersection of Capital Markets, Credit, and Finance. You'll work closely with the Credit and Portfolio Management team and report directly to the CFO.

 - Title: Capital Markets Manager

 - Reports to: Chief Financial Officer

 - Location: New York, NY

 - Type: Full-time




WHAT YOU'LL DO



DEBT FACILITY MANAGEMENT & REPORTING



LENDER REPORTING

 - Own the monthly and periodic reporting cycle: borrowing base certificates, loan-level portfolio tapes, servicing reports, and compliance certificates.

 - Deliver every report accurately and on time, with a documented close checklist and review controls.

 - Prepare ad hoc analyses for lenders on portfolio performance, concentrations, and credit trends.


COVENANT AND ELIGIBILITY MONITORING

 - Test eligibility criteria, concentration limits, advance rates, and performance triggers each cycle.

 - Track excess spread, delinquency, and loss triggers, and flag any approaching breach to the CFO early.

 - Keep a covenant calendar covering every reporting deadline, certification, and notice requirement.


FUNDING AND CASH MANAGEMENT

 - Manage draws, paydowns, and the pledging of eligible receivables into the facility.

 - Reconcile facility balances, interest, and fees against the loan ledger and bank accounts.

 - Forecast borrowing base availability and liquidity so the lending book never outruns its funding.


LENDER AND STAKEHOLDER RELATIONSHIPS

 - Act as day-to-day contact for lenders, backup servicers, verification agents, and auditors.

 - Coordinate data requests, field exams, and audits.

 - Support facility raises, amendments, and upsizes: data room prep, diligence responses, and document review alongside counsel.


PROCESS AND TOOLING

 - Build and maintain the facility model.

 - Automate data pulls and report production as the portfolio scales.




WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

Required

 - 2–4 years in capital markets, structured finance, or lender finance, ideally at a specialty lender, fintech, or warehouse lender.

 - Direct experience preparing borrowing base certificates, covenant tests, and portfolio tapes for a credit facility.

 - Working knowledge of warehouse or asset-based facility mechanics: eligibility, advance rates, concentration limits, and triggers.

 - Advanced Excel / Google Sheets skills, including building and maintaining facility models.

 - Solid grasp of GAAP financial statements and how lending activity flows through them.

 - Exceptional attention to detail; you treat a lender report like a legal document.

 - Clear communicator, comfortable working directly with lenders and the CFO.

 - Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field.

Nice to Have

 - SQL or Python for pulling and reconciling loan-level data.

 - Experience with revolving credit, receivables, or card products.

 - Exposure to a facility raise or amendment from term sheet to close.

 - Familiarity with credit agreements and the ability to translate legal terms into reporting logic.

 - CPA, CFA (or progress toward), or MBA.

You'll thrive at Highbeam if...

 - You love working in-person with a high-performing team

 - You enjoy working in an idea-meritocratic, low-ego environment

 - You are proactive and self-directed, and you excel in ambiguous, fast moving environments

 - You care about delivering a polished customer experience

 - Bonus: You have experience working in fintech, AI or early-stage startups



What we offer

 - Competitive salary and meaningful equity

 - Comprehensive health & benefits package

 - Generous PTO

 - $1K/year stipend to purchase our customers' products

 - $100/mo wellness stipend

 - Yearly offsite—last year we went to Mexico City!

 - In-office perks: Commute covered and $20/day lunch stipend

 - Great location: Our NYC office is in NoHo, a short walk from the A,C,E · B,D,F,M · N,Q,R,W · 1 · 6 trains. Our Toronto office is downtown near St. Andrew Station.

title: Commercial Strategy & Operations Specialist
description:
About Flatpay 
 Flatpay is not just another payment solution; we're dedicated to innovating the market for payment solutions and financial services in the SME segment with our customer-centric and transparent services. 
 We've grown into one of the fastest-growing fintech companies out of the Nordics and Denmark's fastest unicorn company. Today, we're more than 2,000 colleagues across Europe, building products that make a real difference for our customers. We've recently launched in the US and are looking for the first people to join our rocket ship out of New York! 
 We're ambitious, move fast, and like to challenge the status quo - but we also believe work should be fun. We celebrate wins, help each other out, and create an environment where people can do great work while genuinely enjoying the journey. 
 What you'll do 
 We’re looking for a Commercial Strategy & Operations Specialist to join us as a trusted partner to the Commercial Director, leading strategic and operational projects across our Field Sales and Marketing Contact Center (MCC) teams. You’ll tackle the questions that shape our growth: where to expand, how to structure our teams, and how to convert more calls and meetings into active merchants. You’ll take projects from first analysis through to delivery, working side by side with Field Sales and MCC leadership, as well as colleagues in Operations, Product, Finance and Recruitment. The role blends rigorous analysis with real time alongside our sales teams, so you can turn insights into practical improvements and results you can measure. 
 Main responsibilities 
- Shape our expansion strategy and launch plans. Assess new markets, prioritize territories and build launch plans covering recruitment, sales capacity, operational readiness and sequencing 
- Build scalable sales structures. Develop territory coverage, capacity models and ways of working across Field Sales and MCC, aligning meeting generation with sales capacity. 
- Strengthen sales enablement . Drive improvements to sales tools, playbooks, onboarding, training and incentive structures, helping sellers and bookers become productive faster. 
- Improve both commercial funnels. Optimize the MCC funnel from calls to qualified bookings and the Field Sales funnel from meetings to signed and activated merchants. Identify bottlenecks, test solutions and scale what works. 
- Turn performance data into action. Analyze KPIs such as call-to-book conversion, meeting-to-sale conversion, productivity, ramp-up, activation and acquisition payback. Translate findings into clear priorities and actions. 
- Drive operational improvements. Improve processes and handoffs across booking, sales, merchant onboarding, and installation. Align stakeholders, set milestones, and follow projects through delivery. 
 Skills & Attributes 
- 2+ years of full-time experience in fintech, management consulting, venture capital or a similar analytical, commercial environment. 
- You’re strong with numbers. You’re at ease with large datasets, build robust analyses, and check your own work before it goes out. You’re confident in Excel and can turn findings into clear, compelling presentations. 
- You can structure an open-ended problem. You break big questions into their parts, focus on what matters and explain your conclusions clearly, both in writing and out loud. 
- You take ownership and follow through. You’re happy to drive projects independently, bring colleagues together and make sure recommendations turn into real improvements. 
- You pair commercial judgement with curiosity. You want to understand what drives sales performance, merchant value and sustainable unit economics, and you’re willing to get close to the operation to find the answers. 
- You collaborate effectively. You’re a confident communicator, build productive relationships across functions, and take a humble, team-first approach. 
- You’re comfortable with AI tools. You use them in your day-to-day work to analyze data, summarize information and automate repetitive tasks, and you know when to trust the output and when to check it.
- You don’t need to know everything from day one. We’re looking for someone curious, eager to learn, and ready to take responsibility. 
 Why Flatpay 
 Joining Flatpay means stepping into a dynamic environment where innovation is encouraged, and teamwork is celebrated. Here, you'll have the opportunity to make a meaningful impact, contributing to our mission of empowering merchants to succeed. 
 With us, you’ll experience an ambitious drive to constantly push boundaries and redefine what's possible. While we don’t take ourselves too seriously, we take our responsibility towards our people very seriously. We welcome driven, low-ego individuals who live our values and want to grow with us. 
 At Flatpay, how we work matters as much as what we achieve. 
- Happy Humans – We bring energy to our work and create teams people enjoy being part of. 
- No Assholes – We perform at a high level while treating colleagues and customers with respect. 
- It’s Our Business, Own It – Everyone takes responsibility and manages their work like it’s their own business. 
- Start With No – We challenge ideas, think commercially and focus on what truly creates value. 
- Sky-High Ambitions – We set bold goals and expect people to keep raising the bar. 
- The Best Argument Wins – Titles don’t decide outcomes. We debate openly to reach the best decisions. 
 Competitive salary, standard US benefits - including health insurance and 401(K). 
 Salary Range - $75,000 - $110,000 
 Location 
 This is an on-site role based in our Midtown, NYC office. Relocation is not provided

About Aquarian

Aquarian Holdings ("Aquarian") is a diversified global holding company with a strategic portfolio of insurance and asset management solutions.



Aquarian Insurance Holdings acquires and operates insurance companies with a focus on life and annuity underwriting, deploying strategies to grow balance sheet profitability by writing new insurance/reinsurance, improving investment income, and optimizing operations. After launching in 2017, Aquarian finalized its first investment in 2018 in Investors Heritage, a regional life insurer domiciled in Kentucky that focuses on pre-need policies. Working closely with management, Aquarian helped the company grow with expanded product offerings and distribution channels, building on its 60-year track record of exceptional client service.



Aquarian continued to deepen its expertise and grow its existing offerings in insurance and reinsurance through its acquisitions of Hudson Life and Annuity Company in 2021 and Somerset Re in 2022.



Aquarian Investments complements the insurance operations , combining best practices from the world’s leading financial services firms with its own distinct strategy, approach, and organizational culture. Aquarian has continued to expand into alternative assets and private credit through the launches of Aquarian Liquid Credit, Aquarian Strategic Opportunities, Aquarian Private Credit, and Aquarian Real Estate Partners.



Aquarian has since grown its business to approximately $25.8 billion in AUM, with 40 investment professionals, multiple funds, and insurance and reinsurance companies, all committed to providing meaningful investment opportunities to millions of people.



In November 2025, Aquarian announced the signing of a definitive merger agreement under which an affiliate will acquire Brighthouse Financial in an all-cash transaction valued at approximately $4.1 billion. Brighthouse is one of the largest providers of annuities and life insurance in the U.S., with approximately $208 billion of AUM. Following the anticipated close of the transaction in 2026, Brighthouse Financial will operate as a standalone entity within the Aquarian portfolio.



Role Summary

Aquarian Holdings is seeking a highly motivated, detail-oriented Corporate Development Associate with Financial Institutions Group (FIG) investment banking and/or private equity experience to support the Corporate Development and Aquarian Strategic Opportunities (ASO) teams. The Associate will play an active role in evaluating and executing strategic transactions and investments across the Aquarian platform, with exposure to M&A, transaction analysis, financial modeling, due diligence, execution, and ongoing portfolio monitoring.

The Associate will report to Corporate Development leadership and work closely with the ASO team and other senior leaders across the organization on strategic initiatives and transactions. The role provides significant exposure across the Aquarian platform, direct engagement with senior decision makers, and the opportunity to take on progressively greater responsibility. For high-performing individuals, we expect the role to provide meaningful advancement opportunities within the firm.

The position is based in New York City with an immediate start date.

 - Conduct financial, market, and industry analysis to evaluate potential acquisitions, investments, and other strategic opportunities.

 - Support all aspects of transaction due diligence, working closely with internal teams and external advisors to evaluate potential targets and investment opportunities.

 - Support transaction execution, including the negotiation and development of term sheets, transaction documentation, and other legal materials.
 - Coordinate and, in certain instances, lead workstreams with external advisors, including investment bankers, attorneys, consultants, and third-party diligence providers.
 - Monitor industry trends, competitive dynamics, and regulatory developments across the financial services sector.
 - Support ongoing monitoring and oversight of completed transactions and investments, including periodic and ad hoc analysis.
 - Partner with teams across the organization, including Legal, Investment Operations, and Finance to ensure timely completion of fundings and regulatory compliance.
Qualifications:
 - 3–5 years of relevant experience in investment banking and/or private equity, including meaningful FIG experience, with M&A, structured finance, and/or leveraged finance experience strongly preferred.
 - Robust skills in Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint, with proficiency in other Microsoft Office applications, as well as financial services applications such as Capital IQ, Bloomberg, etc.
 - Intermediate understanding of credit investing is a plus.
We desire the following qualities in all candidates:
 - Must be detail-oriented and have excellent analytical and presentation skills.
 - Must possess strong critical thinking skills, a high degree of intellectual curiosity, and a desire to take on greater responsibilities and leadership, all of which are essential to success at Aquarian.

 AQR’s culture reflects the firm’s academic roots and entrepreneurial spirit. Our collaborative environment fuels innovation and encourages employees to ask thoughtful questions, think creatively and bring new ideas forward. Continuous learning is an important part of the employee experience, helping our people build skills and grow throughout their careers. Employees at every level have opportunities to contribute, regardless of title or tenure.
 The firm has 800 employees with headquarters in Greenwich, Connecticut and offices in London, Frankfurt, Dubai, Hong Kong, Sydney and Bengaluru.
 The Team 
 AQR is looking to hire a full-time Associate on our U.S. Wealth Team, within the Business Development group in a Business Development Strategy role. The Business Development group works with AQR’s clients in North America, Europe, Australia and the Middle East to provide solutions to achieve their investment objectives. - Build them on the domain SOPs owned by the Managers of Risk and Recovery Program Operations; domain SOPs stay with their owners

description:
Mission Lane is combining the power of data, technology, and exceptional service to pave a clear way forward for millions of people on the path to financial success. By attracting top talent and leveraging cutting-edge technology, we’re enabling people to unlock real financial progress. Sound like a mission you can get behind?
 We're looking for a Business Manager to own the outcomes of our credit line increase program, reporting to the Director, Portfolio Management. 
 The impact you'll make: 
 A year ago, a customer got her first Mission Lane card with a small credit line. Today she opens the app and sees her line has increased. She’s creating the life she’s working toward, and her card is keeping up with her. Her credit line increase could be a turning point that changes everything.
 As Business Manager, you’ll use your analytical skills and business acumen to make that kind of life-changing forward motion possible for Mission Lane cardholders, every day.
 As Business Manager, CLIP, you will: 
- Use your math and analytical skills to design credit line increase programs, with terms and payments that work for customers’ lives, and model their expected financial impact so our underwriting and pricing decisions support both customer and business success.
- Turn financial data into clear recommendations that grow the business while managing risk responsibly, and present them to senior leadership.
- Design and strengthen the customer lifetime value (LTV) model, so we can see which programs help customers and the business grow together.
- Run small tests in market and use what you learn to adjust our approach as customer behavior and the market change, build insight into how customers behave, and decide where we invest next.
- Partner with product, data science, and engineering to bring strategies to market, and mentor the analysts working alongside you on the program.
- Get hands-on with AI-driven tools that speed up and sharpen your analysis, so you can test more ideas, find answers sooner, and put better programs in front of customers faster.
 You'll thrive in this role if: 
- You’re motivated by the people behind the numbers, and by knowing that a higher credit line, a better rate, or a manageable payment makes a real difference in a customer’s day-to-day life.
- You’re fascinated by how a card business fits together, from acquisition to risk to engagement, and you enjoy tracing how a change in one part reaches the rest.
- You can’t help digging into the reasoning behind a strategy, down to the assumptions it rests on, because you want to know why it works.
- You like spotting the question nobody has asked yet and picturing where the program should be a year from now.
- You enjoy explaining your thinking clearly enough that someone outside your team can follow it and get curious about it too.
 Minimum qualifications: 
- 4+ years of experience in a highly analytical role
- A bachelor's or master's degree in economics, finance, engineering, mathematics, or a similarly quantitative field, with a strong academic record
- A track record of leading complex, cross-functional analytical projects from start to finish
- Experience guiding or mentoring other analysts
- Comfort working in SQL, Python, or similar tools for data analysis
- Ability to travel ~4+ times per year for high quality in-person collaboration
 Preferred qualifications: 
- Experience working with credit cards or other consumer lending products
- Experience helping scale a business in a fast-moving startup environment
- Strong SQL or Python skills
- Experience using AI coding assistants (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, etc.)
 Compensation: 
 Annual full-time starting base salary range: $140,000-160,000
 This role is eligible for additional compensation in the forms of participation in our annual incentive and equity programs.
 Pay is based on factors such as work experience, education, certification(s), training, skills, and competencies related to the role. Mission Lane also offers a comprehensive benefits plan, which includes paid time off, 401(k) match, a monthly wellness stipend, health/dental/vision insurance options, disability coverage, paid parental leave, flexible spending account (for childcare and healthcare), life insurance, and a remote-first work environment.
 About Mission Lane: 
 Founded in December 2018, Mission Lane is a purpose-driven fintech company based in the U.S., with headquarters in Richmond, Virginia. 
 [...]  In partnership with our sponsor banks, we offer credit cards under the Mission Lane brand name, with better, clearer terms, and a more refined customer experience than the alternatives available to people working hard to improve their credit. To date, over four million consumers have chosen Mission Lane, earning high customer ratings on Credit Karma for its market segment and industry leading Net Promoter scores. 
 Mission Lane has cumulatively raised over $600 million of equity from leading investors, including Invus Opportunities, QED Investors, LL Funds, funds affiliated with Oaktree Capital Management, and other leading investors.

 Mission Lane is not sponsoring new applicant employment authorization and please, no third-party recruiters.

Lyra Health is a leading provider of evidence-based mental health care, serving more than 20 million people globally in partnership with employers and more than 100 million through health plan and partner relationships. The company has delivered more than 15 million sessions of mental health care, published more than 35 peer-reviewed studies, and delivered unmatched outcomes in terms of access, clinical effectiveness, and cost efficiency.
